b.title: Found 2026-09-17 while writing the node primer: three live sources give three different answers to how many node kinds there are, and all three are correct about different questions. This graph's GRAPH.md, returned by vinc_conventions, lists six under the heading Node kinds: Concept, Episode, Record, Decision, Bridge and Entity, so it counts the open carrier as a kind and does not mention Domain. The vinc_ingest contract says six types route to dedicated tables, record, concept, domain, bridge, episode and decision, and that anything else lands on the Entity carrier, so it counts Domain and excludes Entity. vinc.book.10-architecture.en section 2 says the system knows five kinds structurally, that outside them there is one open place called Entity, and that Domain is a node nobody writes by hand because the system derives it from the slashes in a topic string. The reconciliation is that the book is counting what a person authors, the ingest contract is counting storage tables, and GRAPH.md is counting what a writer may name in a type field. The primer teaches the book's five, names Entity as a carrier rather than a sixth kind, and states that Domain is derived, because a reader choosing a kind is answering the book's question and not the other two.

b.title: Found 2026-09-17 while writing the node primer: three live sources give three different answers to how many node kinds there are, and all three are correct about different questions. This graph's GRAPH.md, returned by vinc_conventions, lists six under the heading Node kinds: Concept, Episode, Record, Decision, Bridge and Entity, so it counts the open carrier as a kind and does not mention Domain. The vinc_ingest contract says six types route to dedicated tables, record, concept, domain, bridge, episode and decision, and that anything else lands on the Entity carrier, so it counts Domain and excludes Entity. vinc.book.10-architecture.en section 2 says the system knows five kinds structurally, that outside them there is one open place called Entity, and that Domain is a node nobody writes by hand because the system derives it from the slashes in a topic string. The reconciliation is that the book is counting what a person authors, the ingest contract is counting storage tables, and GRAPH.md is counting what a writer may name in a type field. The primer teaches the book's five, names Entity as a carrier rather than a sixth kind, and states that Domain is derived, because a reader choosing a kind is answering the book's question and not the other two.

b.title: Written 2026-09-17 under VIN-49 (run oc-20260917-vin49-2): Part 4 (Chapters 29 to 34, slots vinc.book.28-performance to 33-measurement-before-decision) rewritten in Korean and English against the measured corpus rather than against the earlier prose, to the standard Parts 0 to 3 were rewritten to on 2026-09-16. The 2026-09-04 draft argued the right principles from no sources: it carried no chapter numbers, no numbered sections, no chapter-to-chapter hand-offs, spelled Vinc as VINC, used guillemets and em dashes, was filed under vinc/product with part2 tags, and stated its measurements without the runs they came from ("around 25 seconds", "some models took more than three times longer", "as low as 0.472 from 0.670"). Every factual sentence now traces to a graph document. Chapter 29 opens from Chapter 28's Part 3 close and fixes the conditions: the same-fixture rule and the ban on comparing absolute scores across fixtures, the four language axes with ko2en named as load-bearing, the two rounds that measured the wrong thing and said nothing (the first embedding round whose Korean queries were drawn from ASCII titles and filenames and therefore contained zero Korean characters, and the rebuild rehearsal's first evaluation reporting recall 0.0 because the harness read doc_id from a vector_search that returns id), the eleven-item record-these-fields list, the same-moment A/B against two measurements days apart, the cheapest gate first (two candidates screened against their model cards on 2026-09-07 before any fixture was built, both failed, and two of the plan's own premises were wrong), and the rule that a run states what it does not support. Chapter 30 gives calls-to-resolution with latency excluded by definition, the frozen arm policies, the four aggregates (baseline 15 calls 9 useful 40 percent 6 of 7; chain arm 10 calls 40 percent 5 of 7; brief-first 16 calls 62.5 percent 5 of 7; brief with a search in front 20 calls 70 percent), brief as a composite containing search rather than its competitor, target node kind as the axis that displaced question shape (Concept 6 of 6, Decision 2 of 2, Record 0 of 5, Episode 0 of 1) with the status misreporting a loader refusal as a failure to match, the payload crossover at about fifteen links (7,697 B at 0.73 percent used against 1,406 B at 12.66 percent; search flat at 7.7 KB, brief linear at about 455 B per link, the 208-character figure a floor not an envelope), attribution as the axis the chain arm cannot enter at all, and the Record and Episode branches shipped and verified live 2026-09-02 with the title-language tie-break left open by decision. Chapter 31 carries the nDCG@10 table (English-only 0.669/0.347/0.460, multilingual 0.636/0.670/0.658, vendor int8 0.574/0.472/0.508) stated as a trade rather than an improvement, the vendor int8 collapse traced to quantization without range reduction saturating the accumulator on a processor without the newer instruction extension and the self-built rebuild restoring Korean to 0.669, parent-and-child vectors with averaging measured below baseline (0.535 against 0.601 and 0.659) and the link-loss window that inflates links by up to 137 percent instead of restoring them, the cross-lingual numbers from the rebuild rehearsal, the artifact table with the 570 MB against 2.27 GB floor in a one-gibibyte container, and two honest notes: the cross-encoder is measured and not deployed pending a second container, and the 1024-dimensional candidate is ruled adopted with execution remaining while the shipped model is still 768. Chapter 32 prices the change: the dimension as a storage contract, provision at the new width returning all 31 statements and raising nothing while leaving the column where it was, the conversion error arriving only after every vector has already been deleted, the desktop vector table structurally empty so the fleet rebuild is one hub store, the four-step rebuild contract, the same-moment A/B where correctness cost 2.57 seconds against a refill of 410 to 1345 seconds, the encode bill (0.80 against 0.23 chunks per second, 3.5x, roughly 1.8 hours for 1500 chunks and 12 hours for 10,000), concurrency memory-bound at about 83 percent scaling, rollback as another rebuild with zero metadata mismatches after two of them, interruption safety once index build moved before re-embedding, and the metadata gap that was larger than the rebuild because backup restore and device migration had been losing the same tables all along. Chapter 33 collects the silent failures: the arm that did not run (8 fused, 4 timed out), the top-agree gate that fired 0 times in 75 queries because its threshold was pinned to a module constant of 60 against a pool production fuses at 20, and which once fixed skips 11 of 75 with numbers identical to always-reranking to three decimals, the status that misreported its own failure and the fix that moved it from loud to silent with a characterization test asserting the wrong answer, the edge evidence accepted and dropped with empty warnings and no partial flag, the English twin of Chapter 28 stored cut off mid-sentence in section 4 of 8 and reading as prose, the validity filter that turned an honest choose into an unearned resolved on one of six unanswerable questions, do not pick when it is ambiguous, and recovery as a measured axis. Chapter 34 gives the ordering: the decision its own conditions overturned, the measurement gate between result and decision, the six questions that precede it, the corrected recommendation list that ranked the symptom above the cause because it was proposed without reading the code, a plan's premises decaying like any other claim, the output being a record first and a decision second, the same ordering inside an Agent, and Part 4's mixed verdicts stated as mixed. All fourteen documents were read back after writing and each returned verified true on its first read with no truncation. Slot numbers still diverge from chapter numbers after Chapter 22, so the Chapter column of vinc.book.index remains the authority. Topics are authored at write time (vinc/product/book/part2 for Chapters 29 to 34), Vinc is spelled Vinc, and the English twins carry no em dash.

b.title: Written 2026-09-17 under VIN-49 (run oc-20260917-vin49-2): Part 4 (Chapters 29 to 34, slots vinc.book.28-performance to 33-measurement-before-decision) rewritten in Korean and English against the measured corpus rather than against the earlier prose, to the standard Parts 0 to 3 were rewritten to on 2026-09-16. The 2026-09-04 draft argued the right principles from no sources: it carried no chapter numbers, no numbered sections, no chapter-to-chapter hand-offs, spelled Vinc as VINC, used guillemets and em dashes, was filed under vinc/product with part2 tags, and stated its measurements without the runs they came from ("around 25 seconds", "some models took more than three times longer", "as low as 0.472 from 0.670"). Every factual sentence now traces to a graph document. Chapter 29 opens from Chapter 28's Part 3 close and fixes the conditions: the same-fixture rule and the ban on comparing absolute scores across fixtures, the four language axes with ko2en named as load-bearing, the two rounds that measured the wrong thing and said nothing (the first embedding round whose Korean queries were drawn from ASCII titles and filenames and therefore contained zero Korean characters, and the rebuild rehearsal's first evaluation reporting recall 0.0 because the harness read doc_id from a vector_search that returns id), the eleven-item record-these-fields list, the same-moment A/B against two measurements days apart, the cheapest gate first (two candidates screened against their model cards on 2026-09-07 before any fixture was built, both failed, and two of the plan's own premises were wrong), and the rule that a run states what it does not support. Chapter 30 gives calls-to-resolution with latency excluded by definition, the frozen arm policies, the four aggregates (baseline 15 calls 9 useful 40 percent 6 of 7; chain arm 10 calls 40 percent 5 of 7; brief-first 16 calls 62.5 percent 5 of 7; brief with a search in front 20 calls 70 percent), brief as a composite containing search rather than its competitor, target node kind as the axis that displaced question shape (Concept 6 of 6, Decision 2 of 2, Record 0 of 5, Episode 0 of 1) with the status misreporting a loader refusal as a failure to match, the payload crossover at about fifteen links (7,697 B at 0.73 percent used against 1,406 B at 12.66 percent; search flat at 7.7 KB, brief linear at about 455 B per link, the 208-character figure a floor not an envelope), attribution as the axis the chain arm cannot enter at all, and the Record and Episode branches shipped and verified live 2026-09-02 with the title-language tie-break left open by decision. Chapter 31 carries the nDCG@10 table (English-only 0.669/0.347/0.460, multilingual 0.636/0.670/0.658, vendor int8 0.574/0.472/0.508) stated as a trade rather than an improvement, the vendor int8 collapse traced to quantization without range reduction saturating the accumulator on a processor without the newer instruction extension and the self-built rebuild restoring Korean to 0.669, parent-and-child vectors with averaging measured below baseline (0.535 against 0.601 and 0.659) and the link-loss window that inflates links by up to 137 percent instead of restoring them, the cross-lingual numbers from the rebuild rehearsal, the artifact table with the 570 MB against 2.27 GB floor in a one-gibibyte container, and two honest notes: the cross-encoder is measured and not deployed pending a second container, and the 1024-dimensional candidate is ruled adopted with execution remaining while the shipped model is still 768. Chapter 32 prices the change: the dimension as a storage contract, provision at the new width returning all 31 statements and raising nothing while leaving the column where it was, the conversion error arriving only after every vector has already been deleted, the desktop vector table structurally empty so the fleet rebuild is one hub store, the four-step rebuild contract, the same-moment A/B where correctness cost 2.57 seconds against a refill of 410 to 1345 seconds, the encode bill (0.80 against 0.23 chunks per second, 3.5x, roughly 1.8 hours for 1500 chunks and 12 hours for 10,000), concurrency memory-bound at about 83 percent scaling, rollback as another rebuild with zero metadata mismatches after two of them, interruption safety once index build moved before re-embedding, and the metadata gap that was larger than the rebuild because backup restore and device migration had been losing the same tables all along. Chapter 33 collects the silent failures: the arm that did not run (8 fused, 4 timed out), the top-agree gate that fired 0 times in 75 queries because its threshold was pinned to a module constant of 60 against a pool production fuses at 20, and which once fixed skips 11 of 75 with numbers identical to always-reranking to three decimals, the status that misreported its own failure and the fix that moved it from loud to silent with a characterization test asserting the wrong answer, the edge evidence accepted and dropped with empty warnings and no partial flag, the English twin of Chapter 28 stored cut off mid-sentence in section 4 of 8 and reading as prose, the validity filter that turned an honest choose into an unearned resolved on one of six unanswerable questions, do not pick when it is ambiguous, and recovery as a measured axis. Chapter 34 gives the ordering: the decision its own conditions overturned, the measurement gate between result and decision, the six questions that precede it, the corrected recommendation list that ranked the symptom above the cause because it was proposed without reading the code, a plan's premises decaying like any other claim, the output being a record first and a decision second, the same ordering inside an Agent, and Part 4's mixed verdicts stated as mixed. All fourteen documents were read back after writing and each returned verified true on its first read with no truncation. Slot numbers still diverge from chapter numbers after Chapter 22, so the Chapter column of vinc.book.index remains the authority. Topics are authored at write time (vinc/product/book/part2 for Chapters 29 to 34), Vinc is spelled Vinc, and the English twins carry no em dash.

b.title: Measured 2026-09-17 on /docs/concepts/ at Vinc-homepage 8ba33f4: the chosen primer shape and the five-minute reading target do not both fit, and the target is the one that gave way. The first full draft measured 1970 words of body text, about 8.6 minutes at 230 words per minute; one cutting pass took it to 1651 words, about 7.2 minutes. Getting to the roughly 1150 words that five minutes buys would mean dropping one of the four elements from each of the six primitives, and those four elements are criteria E1 to E4, which VIN-50 tests, whereas the five minutes is prose in plan section 4.2 and is not a numbered criterion. So four elements times six primitives won and the target was reported missed. The general shape worth carrying: when a plan states a size target and a criteria table states a content requirement, only one of them is machine-checked, and the unchecked one is the one that silently gets met by damaging the checked one unless the tension is measured and named.

b.title: Found 2026-09-17 while writing the node primer: three live sources give three different answers to how many node kinds there are, and all three are correct about different questions. This graph's GRAPH.md, returned by vinc_conventions, lists six under the heading Node kinds: Concept, Episode, Record, Decision, Bridge and Entity, so it counts the open carrier as a kind and does not mention Domain. The vinc_ingest contract says six types route to dedicated tables, record, concept, domain, bridge, episode and decision, and that anything else lands on the Entity carrier, so it counts Domain and excludes Entity. vinc.book.10-architecture.en section 2 says the system knows five kinds structurally, that outside them there is one open place called Entity, and that Domain is a node nobody writes by hand because the system derives it from the slashes in a topic string. The reconciliation is that the book is counting what a person authors, the ingest contract is counting storage tables, and GRAPH.md is counting what a writer may name in a type field. The primer teaches the book's five, names Entity as a carrier rather than a sixth kind, and states that Domain is derived, because a reader choosing a kind is answering the book's question and not the other two.

b.title: Written 2026-09-17 under VIN-49 (run oc-20260917-vin49-2): Part 4 (Chapters 29 to 34, slots vinc.book.28-performance to 33-measurement-before-decision) rewritten in Korean and English against the measured corpus rather than against the earlier prose, to the standard Parts 0 to 3 were rewritten to on 2026-09-16. The 2026-09-04 draft argued the right principles from no sources: it carried no chapter numbers, no numbered sections, no chapter-to-chapter hand-offs, spelled Vinc as VINC, used guillemets and em dashes, was filed under vinc/product with part2 tags, and stated its measurements without the runs they came from ("around 25 seconds", "some models took more than three times longer", "as low as 0.472 from 0.670"). Every factual sentence now traces to a graph document. Chapter 29 opens from Chapter 28's Part 3 close and fixes the conditions: the same-fixture rule and the ban on comparing absolute scores across fixtures, the four language axes with ko2en named as load-bearing, the two rounds that measured the wrong thing and said nothing (the first embedding round whose Korean queries were drawn from ASCII titles and filenames and therefore contained zero Korean characters, and the rebuild rehearsal's first evaluation reporting recall 0.0 because the harness read doc_id from a vector_search that returns id), the eleven-item record-these-fields list, the same-moment A/B against two measurements days apart, the cheapest gate first (two candidates screened against their model cards on 2026-09-07 before any fixture was built, both failed, and two of the plan's own premises were wrong), and the rule that a run states what it does not support. Chapter 30 gives calls-to-resolution with latency excluded by definition, the frozen arm policies, the four aggregates (baseline 15 calls 9 useful 40 percent 6 of 7; chain arm 10 calls 40 percent 5 of 7; brief-first 16 calls 62.5 percent 5 of 7; brief with a search in front 20 calls 70 percent), brief as a composite containing search rather than its competitor, target node kind as the axis that displaced question shape (Concept 6 of 6, Decision 2 of 2, Record 0 of 5, Episode 0 of 1) with the status misreporting a loader refusal as a failure to match, the payload crossover at about fifteen links (7,697 B at 0.73 percent used against 1,406 B at 12.66 percent; search flat at 7.7 KB, brief linear at about 455 B per link, the 208-character figure a floor not an envelope), attribution as the axis the chain arm cannot enter at all, and the Record and Episode branches shipped and verified live 2026-09-02 with the title-language tie-break left open by decision. Chapter 31 carries the nDCG@10 table (English-only 0.669/0.347/0.460, multilingual 0.636/0.670/0.658, vendor int8 0.574/0.472/0.508) stated as a trade rather than an improvement, the vendor int8 collapse traced to quantization without range reduction saturating the accumulator on a processor without the newer instruction extension and the self-built rebuild restoring Korean to 0.669, parent-and-child vectors with averaging measured below baseline (0.535 against 0.601 and 0.659) and the link-loss window that inflates links by up to 137 percent instead of restoring them, the cross-lingual numbers from the rebuild rehearsal, the artifact table with the 570 MB against 2.27 GB floor in a one-gibibyte container, and two honest notes: the cross-encoder is measured and not deployed pending a second container, and the 1024-dimensional candidate is ruled adopted with execution remaining while the shipped model is still 768. Chapter 32 prices the change: the dimension as a storage contract, provision at the new width returning all 31 statements and raising nothing while leaving the column where it was, the conversion error arriving only after every vector has already been deleted, the desktop vector table structurally empty so the fleet rebuild is one hub store, the four-step rebuild contract, the same-moment A/B where correctness cost 2.57 seconds against a refill of 410 to 1345 seconds, the encode bill (0.80 against 0.23 chunks per second, 3.5x, roughly 1.8 hours for 1500 chunks and 12 hours for 10,000), concurrency memory-bound at about 83 percent scaling, rollback as another rebuild with zero metadata mismatches after two of them, interruption safety once index build moved before re-embedding, and the metadata gap that was larger than the rebuild because backup restore and device migration had been losing the same tables all along. Chapter 33 collects the silent failures: the arm that did not run (8 fused, 4 timed out), the top-agree gate that fired 0 times in 75 queries because its threshold was pinned to a module constant of 60 against a pool production fuses at 20, and which once fixed skips 11 of 75 with numbers identical to always-reranking to three decimals, the status that misreported its own failure and the fix that moved it from loud to silent with a characterization test asserting the wrong answer, the edge evidence accepted and dropped with empty warnings and no partial flag, the English twin of Chapter 28 stored cut off mid-sentence in section 4 of 8 and reading as prose, the validity filter that turned an honest choose into an unearned resolved on one of six unanswerable questions, do not pick when it is ambiguous, and recovery as a measured axis. Chapter 34 gives the ordering: the decision its own conditions overturned, the measurement gate between result and decision, the six questions that precede it, the corrected recommendation list that ranked the symptom above the cause because it was proposed without reading the code, a plan's premises decaying like any other claim, the output being a record first and a decision second, the same ordering inside an Agent, and Part 4's mixed verdicts stated as mixed. All fourteen documents were read back after writing and each returned verified true on its first read with no truncation. Slot numbers still diverge from chapter numbers after Chapter 22, so the Chapter column of vinc.book.index remains the authority. Topics are authored at write time (vinc/product/book/part2 for Chapters 29 to 34), Vinc is spelled Vinc, and the English twins carry no em dash.

b.title: Found 2026-09-17 while writing the node primer: three live sources give three different answers to how many node kinds there are, and all three are correct about different questions. This graph's GRAPH.md, returned by vinc_conventions, lists six under the heading Node kinds: Concept, Episode, Record, Decision, Bridge and Entity, so it counts the open carrier as a kind and does not mention Domain. The vinc_ingest contract says six types route to dedicated tables, record, concept, domain, bridge, episode and decision, and that anything else lands on the Entity carrier, so it counts Domain and excludes Entity. vinc.book.10-architecture.en section 2 says the system knows five kinds structurally, that outside them there is one open place called Entity, and that Domain is a node nobody writes by hand because the system derives it from the slashes in a topic string. The reconciliation is that the book is counting what a person authors, the ingest contract is counting storage tables, and GRAPH.md is counting what a writer may name in a type field. The primer teaches the book's five, names Entity as a carrier rather than a sixth kind, and states that Domain is derived, because a reader choosing a kind is answering the book's question and not the other two.

b.title: Written 2026-09-16: Part 3 (Chapters 24 to 28) rewritten in Korean and English, restructured into numbered sections with each chapter opening from the one before it, and Chapter 24 first working out what Chapter 6 announced and Chapter 18 already used as a search filter. Chapter 24 (`23-temporal`) names the three axes content, graph and valid time; states that an unstated window reads as current rather than historical, measured against the hub the day the policy was adopted (38 percent of Records then carried no start; 747 of 748 had one filled by that evening); splits validity by kind (71 of the 177 live Decisions carried a window as of 2026-09-11, 106 did not); and states two gaps rather than hiding them: document chunks carry no validity and the desktop app draws no interval on any card. Chapter 25 (`24-view`) gives Scope and Viewpoint as two axes neither can move, shape as kind across all four viewpoints with the 2026-08 two-day episode where 2D quietly stopped agreeing with that contract, line width traded for ink density carrying confidence, and the closed-encoding-versus-open-intensity split that decides what a shared pack can and cannot remap. Chapter 26 (`25-space`) states a space is an ownership boundary that needed no schema change, that scope has to sit in both the key and the column on both reads and writes, the three team roles enforced at two points with a build-breaking cross-check between them, and why the team assertion had to be a new type rather than a field added to the old one. Chapter 27 (`26-sync`) fixes the direction convention settled 2026-08-25 (`prerequisite_of` reads forward, `derives_from` and `inherits_from` read backward), the causal cone built from relations rather than a fourth clock, and the verdict order: causal order first, then cones, then density, never a metric. Chapter 28 (`27-infrastructure`) covers topic-driven density from the hub layout preset and the Gaussian verdict (rejected as a way to place Nodes, its radial ramp skipped as redundant with degree, kept only as a proposed overlay layer never deployed). Gap closed 2026-09-16: `vinc.book.27-infrastructure.en`'s stored text had broken off mid-sentence in section 4 of 8 ("...could be mod"); sections 4 through 8 (the rest of the Gaussian verdict, density does not explain cause, layout as a function, proximity is not evidence and density is not importance, and the Part 3 to Part 4 hand-off) were reconstructed from the Korean source and the English twin now reads complete and verified. VINC is spelled Vinc throughout and the English twins carry no em dash where their text survives.

b.title: Written 2026-09-17 under VIN-49 (run oc-20260917-vin49-2): Part 4 (Chapters 29 to 34, slots vinc.book.28-performance to 33-measurement-before-decision) rewritten in Korean and English against the measured corpus rather than against the earlier prose, to the standard Parts 0 to 3 were rewritten to on 2026-09-16. The 2026-09-04 draft argued the right principles from no sources: it carried no chapter numbers, no numbered sections, no chapter-to-chapter hand-offs, spelled Vinc as VINC, used guillemets and em dashes, was filed under vinc/product with part2 tags, and stated its measurements without the runs they came from ("around 25 seconds", "some models took more than three times longer", "as low as 0.472 from 0.670"). Every factual sentence now traces to a graph document. Chapter 29 opens from Chapter 28's Part 3 close and fixes the conditions: the same-fixture rule and the ban on comparing absolute scores across fixtures, the four language axes with ko2en named as load-bearing, the two rounds that measured the wrong thing and said nothing (the first embedding round whose Korean queries were drawn from ASCII titles and filenames and therefore contained zero Korean characters, and the rebuild rehearsal's first evaluation reporting recall 0.0 because the harness read doc_id from a vector_search that returns id), the eleven-item record-these-fields list, the same-moment A/B against two measurements days apart, the cheapest gate first (two candidates screened against their model cards on 2026-09-07 before any fixture was built, both failed, and two of the plan's own premises were wrong), and the rule that a run states what it does not support. Chapter 30 gives calls-to-resolution with latency excluded by definition, the frozen arm policies, the four aggregates (baseline 15 calls 9 useful 40 percent 6 of 7; chain arm 10 calls 40 percent 5 of 7; brief-first 16 calls 62.5 percent 5 of 7; brief with a search in front 20 calls 70 percent), brief as a composite containing search rather than its competitor, target node kind as the axis that displaced question shape (Concept 6 of 6, Decision 2 of 2, Record 0 of 5, Episode 0 of 1) with the status misreporting a loader refusal as a failure to match, the payload crossover at about fifteen links (7,697 B at 0.73 percent used against 1,406 B at 12.66 percent; search flat at 7.7 KB, brief linear at about 455 B per link, the 208-character figure a floor not an envelope), attribution as the axis the chain arm cannot enter at all, and the Record and Episode branches shipped and verified live 2026-09-02 with the title-language tie-break left open by decision. Chapter 31 carries the nDCG@10 table (English-only 0.669/0.347/0.460, multilingual 0.636/0.670/0.658, vendor int8 0.574/0.472/0.508) stated as a trade rather than an improvement, the vendor int8 collapse traced to quantization without range reduction saturating the accumulator on a processor without the newer instruction extension and the self-built rebuild restoring Korean to 0.669, parent-and-child vectors with averaging measured below baseline (0.535 against 0.601 and 0.659) and the link-loss window that inflates links by up to 137 percent instead of restoring them, the cross-lingual numbers from the rebuild rehearsal, the artifact table with the 570 MB against 2.27 GB floor in a one-gibibyte container, and two honest notes: the cross-encoder is measured and not deployed pending a second container, and the 1024-dimensional candidate is ruled adopted with execution remaining while the shipped model is still 768. Chapter 32 prices the change: the dimension as a storage contract, provision at the new width returning all 31 statements and raising nothing while leaving the column where it was, the conversion error arriving only after every vector has already been deleted, the desktop vector table structurally empty so the fleet rebuild is one hub store, the four-step rebuild contract, the same-moment A/B where correctness cost 2.57 seconds against a refill of 410 to 1345 seconds, the encode bill (0.80 against 0.23 chunks per second, 3.5x, roughly 1.8 hours for 1500 chunks and 12 hours for 10,000), concurrency memory-bound at about 83 percent scaling, rollback as another rebuild with zero metadata mismatches after two of them, interruption safety once index build moved before re-embedding, and the metadata gap that was larger than the rebuild because backup restore and device migration had been losing the same tables all along. Chapter 33 collects the silent failures: the arm that did not run (8 fused, 4 timed out), the top-agree gate that fired 0 times in 75 queries because its threshold was pinned to a module constant of 60 against a pool production fuses at 20, and which once fixed skips 11 of 75 with numbers identical to always-reranking to three decimals, the status that misreported its own failure and the fix that moved it from loud to silent with a characterization test asserting the wrong answer, the edge evidence accepted and dropped with empty warnings and no partial flag, the English twin of Chapter 28 stored cut off mid-sentence in section 4 of 8 and reading as prose, the validity filter that turned an honest choose into an unearned resolved on one of six unanswerable questions, do not pick when it is ambiguous, and recovery as a measured axis. Chapter 34 gives the ordering: the decision its own conditions overturned, the measurement gate between result and decision, the six questions that precede it, the corrected recommendation list that ranked the symptom above the cause because it was proposed without reading the code, a plan's premises decaying like any other claim, the output being a record first and a decision second, the same ordering inside an Agent, and Part 4's mixed verdicts stated as mixed. All fourteen documents were read back after writing and each returned verified true on its first read with no truncation. Slot numbers still diverge from chapter numbers after Chapter 22, so the Chapter column of vinc.book.index remains the authority. Topics are authored at write time (vinc/product/book/part2 for Chapters 29 to 34), Vinc is spelled Vinc, and the English twins carry no em dash.

b.title: Written 2026-09-17 under VIN-49 (run oc-20260917-vin49-2): Part 4 (Chapters 29 to 34, slots vinc.book.28-performance to 33-measurement-before-decision) rewritten in Korean and English against the measured corpus rather than against the earlier prose, to the standard Parts 0 to 3 were rewritten to on 2026-09-16. The 2026-09-04 draft argued the right principles from no sources: it carried no chapter numbers, no numbered sections, no chapter-to-chapter hand-offs, spelled Vinc as VINC, used guillemets and em dashes, was filed under vinc/product with part2 tags, and stated its measurements without the runs they came from ("around 25 seconds", "some models took more than three times longer", "as low as 0.472 from 0.670"). Every factual sentence now traces to a graph document. Chapter 29 opens from Chapter 28's Part 3 close and fixes the conditions: the same-fixture rule and the ban on comparing absolute scores across fixtures, the four language axes with ko2en named as load-bearing, the two rounds that measured the wrong thing and said nothing (the first embedding round whose Korean queries were drawn from ASCII titles and filenames and therefore contained zero Korean characters, and the rebuild rehearsal's first evaluation reporting recall 0.0 because the harness read doc_id from a vector_search that returns id), the eleven-item record-these-fields list, the same-moment A/B against two measurements days apart, the cheapest gate first (two candidates screened against their model cards on 2026-09-07 before any fixture was built, both failed, and two of the plan's own premises were wrong), and the rule that a run states what it does not support. Chapter 30 gives calls-to-resolution with latency excluded by definition, the frozen arm policies, the four aggregates (baseline 15 calls 9 useful 40 percent 6 of 7; chain arm 10 calls 40 percent 5 of 7; brief-first 16 calls 62.5 percent 5 of 7; brief with a search in front 20 calls 70 percent), brief as a composite containing search rather than its competitor, target node kind as the axis that displaced question shape (Concept 6 of 6, Decision 2 of 2, Record 0 of 5, Episode 0 of 1) with the status misreporting a loader refusal as a failure to match, the payload crossover at about fifteen links (7,697 B at 0.73 percent used against 1,406 B at 12.66 percent; search flat at 7.7 KB, brief linear at about 455 B per link, the 208-character figure a floor not an envelope), attribution as the axis the chain arm cannot enter at all, and the Record and Episode branches shipped and verified live 2026-09-02 with the title-language tie-break left open by decision. Chapter 31 carries the nDCG@10 table (English-only 0.669/0.347/0.460, multilingual 0.636/0.670/0.658, vendor int8 0.574/0.472/0.508) stated as a trade rather than an improvement, the vendor int8 collapse traced to quantization without range reduction saturating the accumulator on a processor without the newer instruction extension and the self-built rebuild restoring Korean to 0.669, parent-and-child vectors with averaging measured below baseline (0.535 against 0.601 and 0.659) and the link-loss window that inflates links by up to 137 percent instead of restoring them, the cross-lingual numbers from the rebuild rehearsal, the artifact table with the 570 MB against 2.27 GB floor in a one-gibibyte container, and two honest notes: the cross-encoder is measured and not deployed pending a second container, and the 1024-dimensional candidate is ruled adopted with execution remaining while the shipped model is still 768. Chapter 32 prices the change: the dimension as a storage contract, provision at the new width returning all 31 statements and raising nothing while leaving the column where it was, the conversion error arriving only after every vector has already been deleted, the desktop vector table structurally empty so the fleet rebuild is one hub store, the four-step rebuild contract, the same-moment A/B where correctness cost 2.57 seconds against a refill of 410 to 1345 seconds, the encode bill (0.80 against 0.23 chunks per second, 3.5x, roughly 1.8 hours for 1500 chunks and 12 hours for 10,000), concurrency memory-bound at about 83 percent scaling, rollback as another rebuild with zero metadata mismatches after two of them, interruption safety once index build moved before re-embedding, and the metadata gap that was larger than the rebuild because backup restore and device migration had been losing the same tables all along. Chapter 33 collects the silent failures: the arm that did not run (8 fused, 4 timed out), the top-agree gate that fired 0 times in 75 queries because its threshold was pinned to a module constant of 60 against a pool production fuses at 20, and which once fixed skips 11 of 75 with numbers identical to always-reranking to three decimals, the status that misreported its own failure and the fix that moved it from loud to silent with a characterization test asserting the wrong answer, the edge evidence accepted and dropped with empty warnings and no partial flag, the English twin of Chapter 28 stored cut off mid-sentence in section 4 of 8 and reading as prose, the validity filter that turned an honest choose into an unearned resolved on one of six unanswerable questions, do not pick when it is ambiguous, and recovery as a measured axis. Chapter 34 gives the ordering: the decision its own conditions overturned, the measurement gate between result and decision, the six questions that precede it, the corrected recommendation list that ranked the symptom above the cause because it was proposed without reading the code, a plan's premises decaying like any other claim, the output being a record first and a decision second, the same ordering inside an Agent, and Part 4's mixed verdicts stated as mixed. All fourteen documents were read back after writing and each returned verified true on its first read with no truncation. Slot numbers still diverge from chapter numbers after Chapter 22, so the Chapter column of vinc.book.index remains the authority. Topics are authored at write time (vinc/product/book/part2 for Chapters 29 to 34), Vinc is spelled Vinc, and the English twins carry no em dash.

b.title: Written 2026-09-17 under VIN-49 (run oc-20260917-vin49-2): Part 4 (Chapters 29 to 34, slots vinc.book.28-performance to 33-measurement-before-decision) rewritten in Korean and English against the measured corpus rather than against the earlier prose, to the standard Parts 0 to 3 were rewritten to on 2026-09-16. The 2026-09-04 draft argued the right principles from no sources: it carried no chapter numbers, no numbered sections, no chapter-to-chapter hand-offs, spelled Vinc as VINC, used guillemets and em dashes, was filed under vinc/product with part2 tags, and stated its measurements without the runs they came from ("around 25 seconds", "some models took more than three times longer", "as low as 0.472 from 0.670"). Every factual sentence now traces to a graph document. Chapter 29 opens from Chapter 28's Part 3 close and fixes the conditions: the same-fixture rule and the ban on comparing absolute scores across fixtures, the four language axes with ko2en named as load-bearing, the two rounds that measured the wrong thing and said nothing (the first embedding round whose Korean queries were drawn from ASCII titles and filenames and therefore contained zero Korean characters, and the rebuild rehearsal's first evaluation reporting recall 0.0 because the harness read doc_id from a vector_search that returns id), the eleven-item record-these-fields list, the same-moment A/B against two measurements days apart, the cheapest gate first (two candidates screened against their model cards on 2026-09-07 before any fixture was built, both failed, and two of the plan's own premises were wrong), and the rule that a run states what it does not support. Chapter 30 gives calls-to-resolution with latency excluded by definition, the frozen arm policies, the four aggregates (baseline 15 calls 9 useful 40 percent 6 of 7; chain arm 10 calls 40 percent 5 of 7; brief-first 16 calls 62.5 percent 5 of 7; brief with a search in front 20 calls 70 percent), brief as a composite containing search rather than its competitor, target node kind as the axis that displaced question shape (Concept 6 of 6, Decision 2 of 2, Record 0 of 5, Episode 0 of 1) with the status misreporting a loader refusal as a failure to match, the payload crossover at about fifteen links (7,697 B at 0.73 percent used against 1,406 B at 12.66 percent; search flat at 7.7 KB, brief linear at about 455 B per link, the 208-character figure a floor not an envelope), attribution as the axis the chain arm cannot enter at all, and the Record and Episode branches shipped and verified live 2026-09-02 with the title-language tie-break left open by decision. Chapter 31 carries the nDCG@10 table (English-only 0.669/0.347/0.460, multilingual 0.636/0.670/0.658, vendor int8 0.574/0.472/0.508) stated as a trade rather than an improvement, the vendor int8 collapse traced to quantization without range reduction saturating the accumulator on a processor without the newer instruction extension and the self-built rebuild restoring Korean to 0.669, parent-and-child vectors with averaging measured below baseline (0.535 against 0.601 and 0.659) and the link-loss window that inflates links by up to 137 percent instead of restoring them, the cross-lingual numbers from the rebuild rehearsal, the artifact table with the 570 MB against 2.27 GB floor in a one-gibibyte container, and two honest notes: the cross-encoder is measured and not deployed pending a second container, and the 1024-dimensional candidate is ruled adopted with execution remaining while the shipped model is still 768. Chapter 32 prices the change: the dimension as a storage contract, provision at the new width returning all 31 statements and raising nothing while leaving the column where it was, the conversion error arriving only after every vector has already been deleted, the desktop vector table structurally empty so the fleet rebuild is one hub store, the four-step rebuild contract, the same-moment A/B where correctness cost 2.57 seconds against a refill of 410 to 1345 seconds, the encode bill (0.80 against 0.23 chunks per second, 3.5x, roughly 1.8 hours for 1500 chunks and 12 hours for 10,000), concurrency memory-bound at about 83 percent scaling, rollback as another rebuild with zero metadata mismatches after two of them, interruption safety once index build moved before re-embedding, and the metadata gap that was larger than the rebuild because backup restore and device migration had been losing the same tables all along. Chapter 33 collects the silent failures: the arm that did not run (8 fused, 4 timed out), the top-agree gate that fired 0 times in 75 queries because its threshold was pinned to a module constant of 60 against a pool production fuses at 20, and which once fixed skips 11 of 75 with numbers identical to always-reranking to three decimals, the status that misreported its own failure and the fix that moved it from loud to silent with a characterization test asserting the wrong answer, the edge evidence accepted and dropped with empty warnings and no partial flag, the English twin of Chapter 28 stored cut off mid-sentence in section 4 of 8 and reading as prose, the validity filter that turned an honest choose into an unearned resolved on one of six unanswerable questions, do not pick when it is ambiguous, and recovery as a measured axis. Chapter 34 gives the ordering: the decision its own conditions overturned, the measurement gate between result and decision, the six questions that precede it, the corrected recommendation list that ranked the symptom above the cause because it was proposed without reading the code, a plan's premises decaying like any other claim, the output being a record first and a decision second, the same ordering inside an Agent, and Part 4's mixed verdicts stated as mixed. All fourteen documents were read back after writing and each returned verified true on its first read with no truncation. Slot numbers still diverge from chapter numbers after Chapter 22, so the Chapter column of vinc.book.index remains the authority. Topics are authored at write time (vinc/product/book/part2 for Chapters 29 to 34), Vinc is spelled Vinc, and the English twins carry no em dash.

b.title: Measured 2026-08-07: five store tests failed under PowerShell and passed under Git Bash on the same revision and machine, and the shell was a coincidence. The win_amd64 ladybug extensions (algo, fts, vector) need libssl-3-x64.dll and libcrypto-3-x64.dll under exactly those names, but the ladybug wheel ships only delvewheel-mangled copies in ladybug.libs (an upstream mismatch, not a Vinc defect); Git for Windows happens to keep both files unmangled in mingw64/bin, which is on Git Bash's PATH. Putting that directory on PATH makes LOAD EXTENSION vector succeed and settles it. What hid the cause was a second bug: the engine's error text is cp949 and the pybind boundary decoded strict UTF-8, so the real reason turned into a UnicodeDecodeError and vanished; _driver_error_text now recovers the original from UnicodeDecodeError.object and the message names the OpenSSL files and the PATH remedy.

Chapter 24 (`23-temporal`) names the three axes content, graph and valid time; states that an unstated window reads as current rather than historical, measured against the hub the day the policy was adopted (38 percent of Records then carried no start; 747 of 748 had one filled by that evening); splits validity by kind (71 of the 177 live Decisions carried a window as of 2026-09-11, 106 did not); and states two gaps rather than hiding them: document chunks carry no validity and the desktop app draws no interval on any card. b.title: Written 2026-09-17 under VIN-49 (run oc-20260917-vin49-2): Part 4 (Chapters 29 to 34, slots vinc.book.28-performance to 33-measurement-before-decision) rewritten in Korean and English against the measured corpus rather than against the earlier prose, to the standard Parts 0 to 3 were rewritten to on 2026-09-16. The 2026-09-04 draft argued the right principles from no sources: it carried no chapter numbers, no numbered sections, no chapter-to-chapter hand-offs, spelled Vinc as VINC, used guillemets and em dashes, was filed under vinc/product with part2 tags, and stated its measurements without the runs they came from ("around 25 seconds", "some models took more than three times longer", "as low as 0.472 from 0.670"). Every factual sentence now traces to a graph document. Chapter 29 opens from Chapter 28's Part 3 close and fixes the conditions: the same-fixture rule and the ban on comparing absolute scores across fixtures, the four language axes with ko2en named as load-bearing, the two rounds that measured the wrong thing and said nothing (the first embedding round whose Korean queries were drawn from ASCII titles and filenames and therefore contained zero Korean characters, and the rebuild rehearsal's first evaluation reporting recall 0.0 because the harness read doc_id from a vector_search that returns id), the eleven-item record-these-fields list, the same-moment A/B against two measurements days apart, the cheapest gate first (two candidates screened against their model cards on 2026-09-07 before any fixture was built, both failed, and two of the plan's own premises were wrong), and the rule that a run states what it does not support. Chapter 30 gives calls-to-resolution with latency excluded by definition, the frozen arm policies, the four aggregates (baseline 15 calls 9 useful 40 percent 6 of 7; chain arm 10 calls 40 percent 5 of 7; brief-first 16 calls 62.5 percent 5 of 7; brief with a search in front 20 calls 70 percent), brief as a composite containing search rather than its competitor, target node kind as the axis that displaced question shape (Concept 6 of 6, Decision 2 of 2, Record 0 of 5, Episode 0 of 1) with the status misreporting a loader refusal as a failure to match, the payload crossover at about fifteen links (7,697 B at 0.73 percent used against 1,406 B at 12.66 percent; search flat at 7.7 KB, brief linear at about 455 B per link, the 208-character figure a floor not an envelope), attribution as the axis the chain arm cannot enter at all, and the Record and Episode branches shipped and verified live 2026-09-02 with the title-language tie-break left open by decision. Chapter 31 carries the nDCG@10 table (English-only 0.669/0.347/0.460, multilingual 0.636/0.670/0.658, vendor int8 0.574/0.472/0.508) stated as a trade rather than an improvement, the vendor int8 collapse traced to quantization without range reduction saturating the accumulator on a processor without the newer instruction extension and the self-built rebuild restoring Korean to 0.669, parent-and-child vectors with averaging measured below baseline (0.535 against 0.601 and 0.659) and the link-loss window that inflates links by up to 137 percent instead of restoring them, the cross-lingual numbers from the rebuild rehearsal, the artifact table with the 570 MB against 2.27 GB floor in a one-gibibyte container, and two honest notes: the cross-encoder is measured and not deployed pending a second container, and the 1024-dimensional candidate is ruled adopted with execution remaining while the shipped model is still 768. Chapter 32 prices the change: the dimension as a storage contract, provision at the new width returning all 31 statements and raising nothing while leaving the column where it was, the conversion error arriving only after every vector has already been deleted, the desktop vector table structurally empty so the fleet rebuild is one hub store, the four-step rebuild contract, the same-moment A/B where correctness cost 2.57 seconds against a refill of 410 to 1345 seconds, the encode bill (0.80 against 0.23 chunks per second, 3.5x, roughly 1.8 hours for 1500 chunks and 12 hours for 10,000), concurrency memory-bound at about 83 percent scaling, rollback as another rebuild with zero metadata mismatches after two of them, interruption safety once index build moved before re-embedding, and the metadata gap that was larger than the rebuild because backup restore and device migration had been losing the same tables all along. Chapter 33 collects the silent failures: the arm that did not run (8 fused, 4 timed out), the top-agree gate that fired 0 times in 75 queries because its threshold was pinned to a module constant of 60 against a pool production fuses at 20, and which once fixed skips 11 of 75 with numbers identical to always-reranking to three decimals, the status that misreported its own failure and the fix that moved it from loud to silent with a characterization test asserting the wrong answer, the edge evidence accepted and dropped with empty warnings and no partial flag, the English twin of Chapter 28 stored cut off mid-sentence in section 4 of 8 and reading as prose, the validity filter that turned an honest choose into an unearned resolved on one of six unanswerable questions, do not pick when it is ambiguous, and recovery as a measured axis. Chapter 34 gives the ordering: the decision its own conditions overturned, the measurement gate between result and decision, the six questions that precede it, the corrected recommendation list that ranked the symptom above the cause because it was proposed without reading the code, a plan's premises decaying like any other claim, the output being a record first and a decision second, the same ordering inside an Agent, and Part 4's mixed verdicts stated as mixed. All fourteen documents were read back after writing and each returned verified true on its first read with no truncation. Slot numbers still diverge from chapter numbers after Chapter 22, so the Chapter column of vinc.book.index remains the authority. b.title: Written 2026-09-17 under VIN-49 (run oc-20260917-vin49-2): Part 4 (Chapters 29 to 34, slots vinc.book.28-performance to 33-measurement-before-decision) rewritten in Korean and English against the measured corpus rather than against the earlier prose, to the standard Parts 0 to 3 were rewritten to on 2026-09-16. The 2026-09-04 draft argued the right principles from no sources: it carried no chapter numbers, no numbered sections, no chapter-to-chapter hand-offs, spelled Vinc as VINC, used guillemets and em dashes, was filed under vinc/product with part2 tags, and stated its measurements without the runs they came from ("around 25 seconds", "some models took more than three times longer", "as low as 0.472 from 0.670"). Every factual sentence now traces to a graph document. Chapter 29 opens from Chapter 28's Part 3 close and fixes the conditions: the same-fixture rule and the ban on comparing absolute scores across fixtures, the four language axes with ko2en named as load-bearing, the two rounds that measured the wrong thing and said nothing (the first embedding round whose Korean queries were drawn from ASCII titles and filenames and therefore contained zero Korean characters, and the rebuild rehearsal's first evaluation reporting recall 0.0 because the harness read doc_id from a vector_search that returns id), the eleven-item record-these-fields list, the same-moment A/B against two measurements days apart, the cheapest gate first (two candidates screened against their model cards on 2026-09-07 before any fixture was built, both failed, and two of the plan's own premises were wrong), and the rule that a run states what it does not support. Chapter 30 gives calls-to-resolution with latency excluded by definition, the frozen arm policies, the four aggregates (baseline 15 calls 9 useful 40 percent 6 of 7; chain arm 10 calls 40 percent 5 of 7; brief-first 16 calls 62.5 percent 5 of 7; brief with a search in front 20 calls 70 percent), brief as a composite containing search rather than its competitor, target node kind as the axis that displaced question shape (Concept 6 of 6, Decision 2 of 2, Record 0 of 5, Episode 0 of 1) with the status misreporting a loader refusal as a failure to match, the payload crossover at about fifteen links (7,697 B at 0.73 percent used against 1,406 B at 12.66 percent; search flat at 7.7 KB, brief linear at about 455 B per link, the 208-character figure a floor not an envelope), attribution as the axis the chain arm cannot enter at all, and the Record and Episode branches shipped and verified live 2026-09-02 with the title-language tie-break left open by decision. Chapter 31 carries the nDCG@10 table (English-only 0.669/0.347/0.460, multilingual 0.636/0.670/0.658, vendor int8 0.574/0.472/0.508) stated as a trade rather than an improvement, the vendor int8 collapse traced to quantization without range reduction saturating the accumulator on a processor without the newer instruction extension and the self-built rebuild restoring Korean to 0.669, parent-and-child vectors with averaging measured below baseline (0.535 against 0.601 and 0.659) and the link-loss window that inflates links by up to 137 percent instead of restoring them, the cross-lingual numbers from the rebuild rehearsal, the artifact table with the 570 MB against 2.27 GB floor in a one-gibibyte container, and two honest notes: the cross-encoder is measured and not deployed pending a second container, and the 1024-dimensional candidate is ruled adopted with execution remaining while the shipped model is still 768. Chapter 32 prices the change: the dimension as a storage contract, provision at the new width returning all 31 statements and raising nothing while leaving the column where it was, the conversion error arriving only after every vector has already been deleted, the desktop vector table structurally empty so the fleet rebuild is one hub store, the four-step rebuild contract, the same-moment A/B where correctness cost 2.57 seconds against a refill of 410 to 1345 seconds, the encode bill (0.80 against 0.23 chunks per second, 3.5x, roughly 1.8 hours for 1500 chunks and 12 hours for 10,000), concurrency memory-bound at about 83 percent scaling, rollback as another rebuild with zero metadata mismatches after two of them, interruption safety once index build moved before re-embedding, and the metadata gap that was larger than the rebuild because backup restore and device migration had been losing the same tables all along. Chapter 33 collects the silent failures: the arm that did not run (8 fused, 4 timed out), the top-agree gate that fired 0 times in 75 queries because its threshold was pinned to a module constant of 60 against a pool production fuses at 20, and which once fixed skips 11 of 75 with numbers identical to always-reranking to three decimals, the status that misreported its own failure and the fix that moved it from loud to silent with a characterization test asserting the wrong answer, the edge evidence accepted and dropped with empty warnings and no partial flag, the English twin of Chapter 28 stored cut off mid-sentence in section 4 of 8 and reading as prose, the validity filter that turned an honest choose into an unearned resolved on one of six unanswerable questions, do not pick when it is ambiguous, and recovery as a measured axis. Chapter 34 gives the ordering: the decision its own conditions overturned, the measurement gate between result and decision, the six questions that precede it, the corrected recommendation list that ranked the symptom above the cause because it was proposed without reading the code, a plan's premises decaying like any other claim, the output being a record first and a decision second, the same ordering inside an Agent, and Part 4's mixed verdicts stated as mixed. All fourteen documents were read back after writing and each returned verified true on its first read with no truncation. Slot numbers still diverge from chapter numbers after Chapter 22, so the Chapter column of vinc.book.index remains the authority. Topics are authored at write time (vinc/product/book/part2 for Chapters 29 to 34), Vinc is spelled Vinc, and the English twins carry no em dash.

b.title: Failure traced 2026-09-11: an agent reported bge-m3 adoption as an open question and offered to author the decision, when decision:bge-m3-adoption had approved it on 2026-08-30 and only condition 7 of the separate execution decision was open. The source was one clause of a plan document that compresses both decisions into 'approved in principle, waits on the owner's ruling', which is true and reads as a single undecided thing. The decision node was one hop away and was never opened, although the same plan's house rule 1 is to read the records before the documents and the agent had transcribed that rule into the document minutes earlier. Two mechanisms, both reusable. First, having read a text closely feels like having verified it: attention on a document tells you what it says, not whether it holds. Second and sharper, the error was expressed as a frame (these two are one decision) rather than a claim, and a frame has no truth value to look up, so it never triggers the check that every falsifiable claim in the same session did trigger. The node had even anticipated the opposite misreading in a prop written for readers, so opening it would have prevented either direction.

b.title: Written 2026-09-16: Part 3 (Chapters 24 to 28) rewritten in Korean and English, restructured into numbered sections with each chapter opening from the one before it, and Chapter 24 first working out what Chapter 6 announced and Chapter 18 already used as a search filter. Chapter 24 (`23-temporal`) names the three axes content, graph and valid time; states that an unstated window reads as current rather than historical, measured against the hub the day the policy was adopted (38 percent of Records then carried no start; 747 of 748 had one filled by that evening); splits validity by kind (71 of the 177 live Decisions carried a window as of 2026-09-11, 106 did not); and states two gaps rather than hiding them: document chunks carry no validity and the desktop app draws no interval on any card. Chapter 25 (`24-view`) gives Scope and Viewpoint as two axes neither can move, shape as kind across all four viewpoints with the 2026-08 two-day episode where 2D quietly stopped agreeing with that contract, line width traded for ink density carrying confidence, and the closed-encoding-versus-open-intensity split that decides what a shared pack can and cannot remap. Chapter 26 (`25-space`) states a space is an ownership boundary that needed no schema change, that scope has to sit in both the key and the column on both reads and writes, the three team roles enforced at two points with a build-breaking cross-check between them, and why the team assertion had to be a new type rather than a field added to the old one. Chapter 27 (`26-sync`) fixes the direction convention settled 2026-08-25 (`prerequisite_of` reads forward, `derives_from` and `inherits_from` read backward), the causal cone built from relations rather than a fourth clock, and the verdict order: causal order first, then cones, then density, never a metric. Chapter 28 (`27-infrastructure`) covers topic-driven density from the hub layout preset and the Gaussian verdict (rejected as a way to place Nodes, its radial ramp skipped as redundant with degree, kept only as a proposed overlay layer never deployed). Gap closed 2026-09-16: `vinc.book.27-infrastructure.en`'s stored text had broken off mid-sentence in section 4 of 8 ("...could be mod"); sections 4 through 8 (the rest of the Gaussian verdict, density does not explain cause, layout as a function, proximity is not evidence and density is not importance, and the Part 3 to Part 4 hand-off) were reconstructed from the Korean source and the English twin now reads complete and verified. VINC is spelled Vinc throughout and the English twins carry no em dash where their text survives.

b.title: Found 2026-09-17 while writing the node primer: three live sources give three different answers to how many node kinds there are, and all three are correct about different questions. This graph's GRAPH.md, returned by vinc_conventions, lists six under the heading Node kinds: Concept, Episode, Record, Decision, Bridge and Entity, so it counts the open carrier as a kind and does not mention Domain. The vinc_ingest contract says six types route to dedicated tables, record, concept, domain, bridge, episode and decision, and that anything else lands on the Entity carrier, so it counts Domain and excludes Entity. vinc.book.10-architecture.en section 2 says the system knows five kinds structurally, that outside them there is one open place called Entity, and that Domain is a node nobody writes by hand because the system derives it from the slashes in a topic string. The reconciliation is that the book is counting what a person authors, the ingest contract is counting storage tables, and GRAPH.md is counting what a writer may name in a type field. The primer teaches the book's five, names Entity as a carrier rather than a sixth kind, and states that Domain is derived, because a reader choosing a kind is answering the book's question and not the other two.

b.title: Found 2026-09-17 while writing the node primer: three live sources give three different answers to how many node kinds there are, and all three are correct about different questions. This graph's GRAPH.md, returned by vinc_conventions, lists six under the heading Node kinds: Concept, Episode, Record, Decision, Bridge and Entity, so it counts the open carrier as a kind and does not mention Domain. The vinc_ingest contract says six types route to dedicated tables, record, concept, domain, bridge, episode and decision, and that anything else lands on the Entity carrier, so it counts Domain and excludes Entity. vinc.book.10-architecture.en section 2 says the system knows five kinds structurally, that outside them there is one open place called Entity, and that Domain is a node nobody writes by hand because the system derives it from the slashes in a topic string. The reconciliation is that the book is counting what a person authors, the ingest contract is counting storage tables, and GRAPH.md is counting what a writer may name in a type field. The primer teaches the book's five, names Entity as a carrier rather than a sixth kind, and states that Domain is derived, because a reader choosing a kind is answering the book's question and not the other two.

b.title: Written 2026-09-16: Part 3 (Chapters 24 to 28) rewritten in Korean and English, restructured into numbered sections with each chapter opening from the one before it, and Chapter 24 first working out what Chapter 6 announced and Chapter 18 already used as a search filter. Chapter 24 (`23-temporal`) names the three axes content, graph and valid time; states that an unstated window reads as current rather than historical, measured against the hub the day the policy was adopted (38 percent of Records then carried no start; 747 of 748 had one filled by that evening); splits validity by kind (71 of the 177 live Decisions carried a window as of 2026-09-11, 106 did not); and states two gaps rather than hiding them: document chunks carry no validity and the desktop app draws no interval on any card. Chapter 25 (`24-view`) gives Scope and Viewpoint as two axes neither can move, shape as kind across all four viewpoints with the 2026-08 two-day episode where 2D quietly stopped agreeing with that contract, line width traded for ink density carrying confidence, and the closed-encoding-versus-open-intensity split that decides what a shared pack can and cannot remap. Chapter 26 (`25-space`) states a space is an ownership boundary that needed no schema change, that scope has to sit in both the key and the column on both reads and writes, the three team roles enforced at two points with a build-breaking cross-check between them, and why the team assertion had to be a new type rather than a field added to the old one. Chapter 27 (`26-sync`) fixes the direction convention settled 2026-08-25 (`prerequisite_of` reads forward, `derives_from` and `inherits_from` read backward), the causal cone built from relations rather than a fourth clock, and the verdict order: causal order first, then cones, then density, never a metric. Chapter 28 (`27-infrastructure`) covers topic-driven density from the hub layout preset and the Gaussian verdict (rejected as a way to place Nodes, its radial ramp skipped as redundant with degree, kept only as a proposed overlay layer never deployed). Gap closed 2026-09-16: `vinc.book.27-infrastructure.en`'s stored text had broken off mid-sentence in section 4 of 8 ("...could be mod"); sections 4 through 8 (the rest of the Gaussian verdict, density does not explain cause, layout as a function, proximity is not evidence and density is not importance, and the Part 3 to Part 4 hand-off) were reconstructed from the Korean source and the English twin now reads complete and verified. VINC is spelled Vinc throughout and the English twins carry no em dash where their text survives.

VINC is spelled Vinc and the English twins carry no em dash.

b.title: Measured 2026-08-07: five store tests failed under PowerShell and passed under Git Bash on the same revision and machine, and the shell was a coincidence. The win_amd64 ladybug extensions (algo, fts, vector) need libssl-3-x64.dll and libcrypto-3-x64.dll under exactly those names, but the ladybug wheel ships only delvewheel-mangled copies in ladybug.libs (an upstream mismatch, not a Vinc defect); Git for Windows happens to keep both files unmangled in mingw64/bin, which is on Git Bash's PATH. Putting that directory on PATH makes LOAD EXTENSION vector succeed and settles it. What hid the cause was a second bug: the engine's error text is cp949 and the pybind boundary decoded strict UTF-8, so the real reason turned into a UnicodeDecodeError and vanished; _driver_error_text now recovers the original from UnicodeDecodeError.object and the message names the OpenSSL files and the PATH remedy.

b.title: Written 2026-09-17 under VIN-49 (run oc-20260917-vin49-2): Part 4 (Chapters 29 to 34, slots vinc.book.28-performance to 33-measurement-before-decision) rewritten in Korean and English against the measured corpus rather than against the earlier prose, to the standard Parts 0 to 3 were rewritten to on 2026-09-16. The 2026-09-04 draft argued the right principles from no sources: it carried no chapter numbers, no numbered sections, no chapter-to-chapter hand-offs, spelled Vinc as VINC, used guillemets and em dashes, was filed under vinc/product with part2 tags, and stated its measurements without the runs they came from ("around 25 seconds", "some models took more than three times longer", "as low as 0.472 from 0.670"). Every factual sentence now traces to a graph document. Chapter 29 opens from Chapter 28's Part 3 close and fixes the conditions: the same-fixture rule and the ban on comparing absolute scores across fixtures, the four language axes with ko2en named as load-bearing, the two rounds that measured the wrong thing and said nothing (the first embedding round whose Korean queries were drawn from ASCII titles and filenames and therefore contained zero Korean characters, and the rebuild rehearsal's first evaluation reporting recall 0.0 because the harness read doc_id from a vector_search that returns id), the eleven-item record-these-fields list, the same-moment A/B against two measurements days apart, the cheapest gate first (two candidates screened against their model cards on 2026-09-07 before any fixture was built, both failed, and two of the plan's own premises were wrong), and the rule that a run states what it does not support. Chapter 30 gives calls-to-resolution with latency excluded by definition, the frozen arm policies, the four aggregates (baseline 15 calls 9 useful 40 percent 6 of 7; chain arm 10 calls 40 percent 5 of 7; brief-first 16 calls 62.5 percent 5 of 7; brief with a search in front 20 calls 70 percent), brief as a composite containing search rather than its competitor, target node kind as the axis that displaced question shape (Concept 6 of 6, Decision 2 of 2, Record 0 of 5, Episode 0 of 1) with the status misreporting a loader refusal as a failure to match, the payload crossover at about fifteen links (7,697 B at 0.73 percent used against 1,406 B at 12.66 percent; search flat at 7.7 KB, brief linear at about 455 B per link, the 208-character figure a floor not an envelope), attribution as the axis the chain arm cannot enter at all, and the Record and Episode branches shipped and verified live 2026-09-02 with the title-language tie-break left open by decision. Chapter 31 carries the nDCG@10 table (English-only 0.669/0.347/0.460, multilingual 0.636/0.670/0.658, vendor int8 0.574/0.472/0.508) stated as a trade rather than an improvement, the vendor int8 collapse traced to quantization without range reduction saturating the accumulator on a processor without the newer instruction extension and the self-built rebuild restoring Korean to 0.669, parent-and-child vectors with averaging measured below baseline (0.535 against 0.601 and 0.659) and the link-loss window that inflates links by up to 137 percent instead of restoring them, the cross-lingual numbers from the rebuild rehearsal, the artifact table with the 570 MB against 2.27 GB floor in a one-gibibyte container, and two honest notes: the cross-encoder is measured and not deployed pending a second container, and the 1024-dimensional candidate is ruled adopted with execution remaining while the shipped model is still 768. Chapter 32 prices the change: the dimension as a storage contract, provision at the new width returning all 31 statements and raising nothing while leaving the column where it was, the conversion error arriving only after every vector has already been deleted, the desktop vector table structurally empty so the fleet rebuild is one hub store, the four-step rebuild contract, the same-moment A/B where correctness cost 2.57 seconds against a refill of 410 to 1345 seconds, the encode bill (0.80 against 0.23 chunks per second, 3.5x, roughly 1.8 hours for 1500 chunks and 12 hours for 10,000), concurrency memory-bound at about 83 percent scaling, rollback as another rebuild with zero metadata mismatches after two of them, interruption safety once index build moved before re-embedding, and the metadata gap that was larger than the rebuild because backup restore and device migration had been losing the same tables all along. Chapter 33 collects the silent failures: the arm that did not run (8 fused, 4 timed out), the top-agree gate that fired 0 times in 75 queries because its threshold was pinned to a module constant of 60 against a pool production fuses at 20, and which once fixed skips 11 of 75 with numbers identical to always-reranking to three decimals, the status that misreported its own failure and the fix that moved it from loud to silent with a characterization test asserting the wrong answer, the edge evidence accepted and dropped with empty warnings and no partial flag, the English twin of Chapter 28 stored cut off mid-sentence in section 4 of 8 and reading as prose, the validity filter that turned an honest choose into an unearned resolved on one of six unanswerable questions, do not pick when it is ambiguous, and recovery as a measured axis. Chapter 34 gives the ordering: the decision its own conditions overturned, the measurement gate between result and decision, the six questions that precede it, the corrected recommendation list that ranked the symptom above the cause because it was proposed without reading the code, a plan's premises decaying like any other claim, the output being a record first and a decision second, the same ordering inside an Agent, and Part 4's mixed verdicts stated as mixed. All fourteen documents were read back after writing and each returned verified true on its first read with no truncation. Slot numbers still diverge from chapter numbers after Chapter 22, so the Chapter column of vinc.book.index remains the authority. Topics are authored at write time (vinc/product/book/part2 for Chapters 29 to 34), Vinc is spelled Vinc, and the English twins carry no em dash.

b.title: Two Vinc test investigations landed on opposite wrong answers before the evidence was in. On 2026-07-27 eleven Windows failures were called local platform behaviour and were in fact real code defects that Linux's permissive file locking had hidden: close() dropped the driver handle instead of closing it, leaving a lock that made re-open return None, and snapshot() copied an open database file. On 2026-08-07 five failures were called a regression and were in fact a missing pair of OpenSSL DLLs. The rule that follows is to reach a minimal reproduction before choosing either label. What was decisive both times was refusing the summary: surfacing the swallowed reason in last_open_error, and reading the PE import table rather than trusting the error text.
