b.title: Written 2026-09-17 under VIN-49 (run oc-20260917-vin49-2): Part 4 (Chapters 29 to 34, slots vinc.book.28-performance to 33-measurement-before-decision) rewritten in Korean and English against the measured corpus rather than against the earlier prose, to the standard Parts 0 to 3 were rewritten to on 2026-09-16. The 2026-09-04 draft argued the right principles from no sources: it carried no chapter numbers, no numbered sections, no chapter-to-chapter hand-offs, spelled Vinc as VINC, used guillemets and em dashes, was filed under vinc/product with part2 tags, and stated its measurements without the runs they came from ("around 25 seconds", "some models took more than three times longer", "as low as 0.472 from 0.670"). Every factual sentence now traces to a graph document. Chapter 29 opens from Chapter 28's Part 3 close and fixes the conditions: the same-fixture rule and the ban on comparing absolute scores across fixtures, the four language axes with ko2en named as load-bearing, the two rounds that measured the wrong thing and said nothing (the first embedding round whose Korean queries were drawn from ASCII titles and filenames and therefore contained zero Korean characters, and the rebuild rehearsal's first evaluation reporting recall 0.0 because the harness read doc_id from a vector_search that returns id), the eleven-item record-these-fields list, the same-moment A/B against two measurements days apart, the cheapest gate first (two candidates screened against their model cards on 2026-09-07 before any fixture was built, both failed, and two of the plan's own premises were wrong), and the rule that a run states what it does not support. Chapter 30 gives calls-to-resolution with latency excluded by definition, the frozen arm policies, the four aggregates (baseline 15 calls 9 useful 40 percent 6 of 7; chain arm 10 calls 40 percent 5 of 7; brief-first 16 calls 62.5 percent 5 of 7; brief with a search in front 20 calls 70 percent), brief as a composite containing search rather than its competitor, target node kind as the axis that displaced question shape (Concept 6 of 6, Decision 2 of 2, Record 0 of 5, Episode 0 of 1) with the status misreporting a loader refusal as a failure to match, the payload crossover at about fifteen links (7,697 B at 0.73 percent used against 1,406 B at 12.66 percent; search flat at 7.7 KB, brief linear at about 455 B per link, the 208-character figure a floor not an envelope), attribution as the axis the chain arm cannot enter at all, and the Record and Episode branches shipped and verified live 2026-09-02 with the title-language tie-break left open by decision. Chapter 31 carries the nDCG@10 table (English-only 0.669/0.347/0.460, multilingual 0.636/0.670/0.658, vendor int8 0.574/0.472/0.508) stated as a trade rather than an improvement, the vendor int8 collapse traced to quantization without range reduction saturating the accumulator on a processor without the newer instruction extension and the self-built rebuild restoring Korean to 0.669, parent-and-child vectors with averaging measured below baseline (0.535 against 0.601 and 0.659) and the link-loss window that inflates links by up to 137 percent instead of restoring them, the cross-lingual numbers from the rebuild rehearsal, the artifact table with the 570 MB against 2.27 GB floor in a one-gibibyte container, and two honest notes: the cross-encoder is measured and not deployed pending a second container, and the 1024-dimensional candidate is ruled adopted with execution remaining while the shipped model is still 768. Chapter 32 prices the change: the dimension as a storage contract, provision at the new width returning all 31 statements and raising nothing while leaving the column where it was, the conversion error arriving only after every vector has already been deleted, the desktop vector table structurally empty so the fleet rebuild is one hub store, the four-step rebuild contract, the same-moment A/B where correctness cost 2.57 seconds against a refill of 410 to 1345 seconds, the encode bill (0.80 against 0.23 chunks per second, 3.5x, roughly 1.8 hours for 1500 chunks and 12 hours for 10,000), concurrency memory-bound at about 83 percent scaling, rollback as another rebuild with zero metadata mismatches after two of them, interruption safety once index build moved before re-embedding, and the metadata gap that was larger than the rebuild because backup restore and device migration had been losing the same tables all along. Chapter 33 collects the silent failures: the arm that did not run (8 fused, 4 timed out), the top-agree gate that fired 0 times in 75 queries because its threshold was pinned to a module constant of 60 against a pool production fuses at 20, and which once fixed skips 11 of 75 with numbers identical to always-reranking to three decimals, the status that misreported its own failure and the fix that moved it from loud to silent with a characterization test asserting the wrong answer, the edge evidence accepted and dropped with empty warnings and no partial flag, the English twin of Chapter 28 stored cut off mid-sentence in section 4 of 8 and reading as prose, the validity filter that turned an honest choose into an unearned resolved on one of six unanswerable questions, do not pick when it is ambiguous, and recovery as a measured axis. Chapter 34 gives the ordering: the decision its own conditions overturned, the measurement gate between result and decision, the six questions that precede it, the corrected recommendation list that ranked the symptom above the cause because it was proposed without reading the code, a plan's premises decaying like any other claim, the output being a record first and a decision second, the same ordering inside an Agent, and Part 4's mixed verdicts stated as mixed. All fourteen documents were read back after writing and each returned verified true on its first read with no truncation. Slot numbers still diverge from chapter numbers after Chapter 22, so the Chapter column of vinc.book.index remains the authority. Topics are authored at write time (vinc/product/book/part2 for Chapters 29 to 34), Vinc is spelled Vinc, and the English twins carry no em dash.

b.title: Written 2026-09-17 under VIN-49 (run oc-20260917-vin49-2): Part 4 (Chapters 29 to 34, slots vinc.book.28-performance to 33-measurement-before-decision) rewritten in Korean and English against the measured corpus rather than against the earlier prose, to the standard Parts 0 to 3 were rewritten to on 2026-09-16. The 2026-09-04 draft argued the right principles from no sources: it carried no chapter numbers, no numbered sections, no chapter-to-chapter hand-offs, spelled Vinc as VINC, used guillemets and em dashes, was filed under vinc/product with part2 tags, and stated its measurements without the runs they came from ("around 25 seconds", "some models took more than three times longer", "as low as 0.472 from 0.670"). Every factual sentence now traces to a graph document. Chapter 29 opens from Chapter 28's Part 3 close and fixes the conditions: the same-fixture rule and the ban on comparing absolute scores across fixtures, the four language axes with ko2en named as load-bearing, the two rounds that measured the wrong thing and said nothing (the first embedding round whose Korean queries were drawn from ASCII titles and filenames and therefore contained zero Korean characters, and the rebuild rehearsal's first evaluation reporting recall 0.0 because the harness read doc_id from a vector_search that returns id), the eleven-item record-these-fields list, the same-moment A/B against two measurements days apart, the cheapest gate first (two candidates screened against their model cards on 2026-09-07 before any fixture was built, both failed, and two of the plan's own premises were wrong), and the rule that a run states what it does not support. Chapter 30 gives calls-to-resolution with latency excluded by definition, the frozen arm policies, the four aggregates (baseline 15 calls 9 useful 40 percent 6 of 7; chain arm 10 calls 40 percent 5 of 7; brief-first 16 calls 62.5 percent 5 of 7; brief with a search in front 20 calls 70 percent), brief as a composite containing search rather than its competitor, target node kind as the axis that displaced question shape (Concept 6 of 6, Decision 2 of 2, Record 0 of 5, Episode 0 of 1) with the status misreporting a loader refusal as a failure to match, the payload crossover at about fifteen links (7,697 B at 0.73 percent used against 1,406 B at 12.66 percent; search flat at 7.7 KB, brief linear at about 455 B per link, the 208-character figure a floor not an envelope), attribution as the axis the chain arm cannot enter at all, and the Record and Episode branches shipped and verified live 2026-09-02 with the title-language tie-break left open by decision. Chapter 31 carries the nDCG@10 table (English-only 0.669/0.347/0.460, multilingual 0.636/0.670/0.658, vendor int8 0.574/0.472/0.508) stated as a trade rather than an improvement, the vendor int8 collapse traced to quantization without range reduction saturating the accumulator on a processor without the newer instruction extension and the self-built rebuild restoring Korean to 0.669, parent-and-child vectors with averaging measured below baseline (0.535 against 0.601 and 0.659) and the link-loss window that inflates links by up to 137 percent instead of restoring them, the cross-lingual numbers from the rebuild rehearsal, the artifact table with the 570 MB against 2.27 GB floor in a one-gibibyte container, and two honest notes: the cross-encoder is measured and not deployed pending a second container, and the 1024-dimensional candidate is ruled adopted with execution remaining while the shipped model is still 768. Chapter 32 prices the change: the dimension as a storage contract, provision at the new width returning all 31 statements and raising nothing while leaving the column where it was, the conversion error arriving only after every vector has already been deleted, the desktop vector table structurally empty so the fleet rebuild is one hub store, the four-step rebuild contract, the same-moment A/B where correctness cost 2.57 seconds against a refill of 410 to 1345 seconds, the encode bill (0.80 against 0.23 chunks per second, 3.5x, roughly 1.8 hours for 1500 chunks and 12 hours for 10,000), concurrency memory-bound at about 83 percent scaling, rollback as another rebuild with zero metadata mismatches after two of them, interruption safety once index build moved before re-embedding, and the metadata gap that was larger than the rebuild because backup restore and device migration had been losing the same tables all along. Chapter 34 gives the ordering: the decision its own conditions overturned, the measurement gate between result and decision, the six questions that precede it, the corrected recommendation list that ranked the symptom above the cause because it was proposed without reading the code, a plan's premises decaying like any other claim, the output being a record first and a decision second, the same ordering inside an Agent, and Part 4's mixed verdicts stated as mixed. All fourteen documents were read back after writing and each returned verified true on its first read with no truncation. b.title: Measured 2026-09-13 on the live account graph: vinc_diagnose(kind=claims) reports conflict_count 233, up from 229 and 230 on 2026-09-12, and three of the new pairs were manufactured by writing four correct records the day before. One new record on vinc:store/embedded_schema.py now pairs as newer against four older records on that path covering mirror keying, ATTACHES_TO evidence, a schema version gap and the schema version number, and all five claims are simultaneously true. The pairing is co-location on a file, not disagreement, because subject_path resolves to a file while a record claims something about an aspect of one. Reading conflicts[].older as a list of invalidation candidates would retire true claims and catch no false ones. This is the second granularity defect on this field after the missing repository prefix, and unlike that one it has no obvious fix, since naming an aspect means coining stable names for parts of files.

b.title: Written 2026-09-16: Part 3 (Chapters 24 to 28) rewritten in Korean and English, restructured into numbered sections with each chapter opening from the one before it, and Chapter 24 first working out what Chapter 6 announced and Chapter 18 already used as a search filter. Chapter 24 (`23-temporal`) names the three axes content, graph and valid time; states that an unstated window reads as current rather than historical, measured against the hub the day the policy was adopted (38 percent of Records then carried no start; 747 of 748 had one filled by that evening); splits validity by kind (71 of the 177 live Decisions carried a window as of 2026-09-11, 106 did not); and states two gaps rather than hiding them: document chunks carry no validity and the desktop app draws no interval on any card. Chapter 25 (`24-view`) gives Scope and Viewpoint as two axes neither can move, shape as kind across all four viewpoints with the 2026-08 two-day episode where 2D quietly stopped agreeing with that contract, line width traded for ink density carrying confidence, and the closed-encoding-versus-open-intensity split that decides what a shared pack can and cannot remap. Chapter 26 (`25-space`) states a space is an ownership boundary that needed no schema change, that scope has to sit in both the key and the column on both reads and writes, the three team roles enforced at two points with a build-breaking cross-check between them, and why the team assertion had to be a new type rather than a field added to the old one. Chapter 27 (`26-sync`) fixes the direction convention settled 2026-08-25 (`prerequisite_of` reads forward, `derives_from` and `inherits_from` read backward), the causal cone built from relations rather than a fourth clock, and the verdict order: causal order first, then cones, then density, never a metric. Chapter 28 (`27-infrastructure`) covers topic-driven density from the hub layout preset and the Gaussian verdict (rejected as a way to place Nodes, its radial ramp skipped as redundant with degree, kept only as a proposed overlay layer never deployed). Gap closed 2026-09-16: `vinc.book.27-infrastructure.en`'s stored text had broken off mid-sentence in section 4 of 8 ("...could be mod"); sections 4 through 8 (the rest of the Gaussian verdict, density does not explain cause, layout as a function, proximity is not evidence and density is not importance, and the Part 3 to Part 4 hand-off) were reconstructed from the Korean source and the English twin now reads complete and verified. VINC is spelled Vinc throughout and the English twins carry no em dash where their text survives.

b.title: Written 2026-09-17 under VIN-49 (run oc-20260917-vin49-2): the closing (Chapter 35, vinc.book.35-cycle) rewritten in Korean and English so that it closes the arc vinc.book.index describes rather than restating it. It now opens from Chapter 34's last line (a measurement does not sit outside the system it measured), restates the storage question as the cycle the index prints, names each part by the problem it closed and the one it left exposed, and argues that no layer makes memory alone by citing Part 4's own findings as cases of one layer being correct while the system was wrong: a resolution path that worked on two node kinds and not the others, a semantic space that doubled one language by giving up part of another, and a gate whose correct-skip and never-fire states printed the same column. The eight questions a memory system must answer structurally are each tied to the mechanism behind them (kinds and relations, the evidence sentence, the fixture and its stated conditions, the failure cases and their dates, the Decision node and its window) instead of standing as a promise. A fourth section was added that the earlier draft had no equivalent for: the book is itself in the graph in both languages, carries its own provenance, goes stale, and several of its chapters were rewritten because the system moved and the text did not, which makes the final claim checkable rather than aspirational. The closing proposition is kept and its em dash removed. Both documents read back verified true on the first read, 3 chunks in English and 2 in Korean, and the topic is authored as vinc/product/book/part3.

b.title: Written 2026-09-16: Part 3 (Chapters 24 to 28) rewritten in Korean and English, restructured into numbered sections with each chapter opening from the one before it, and Chapter 24 first working out what Chapter 6 announced and Chapter 18 already used as a search filter. Chapter 24 (`23-temporal`) names the three axes content, graph and valid time; states that an unstated window reads as current rather than historical, measured against the hub the day the policy was adopted (38 percent of Records then carried no start; 747 of 748 had one filled by that evening); splits validity by kind (71 of the 177 live Decisions carried a window as of 2026-09-11, 106 did not); and states two gaps rather than hiding them: document chunks carry no validity and the desktop app draws no interval on any card. Chapter 25 (`24-view`) gives Scope and Viewpoint as two axes neither can move, shape as kind across all four viewpoints with the 2026-08 two-day episode where 2D quietly stopped agreeing with that contract, line width traded for ink density carrying confidence, and the closed-encoding-versus-open-intensity split that decides what a shared pack can and cannot remap. Chapter 26 (`25-space`) states a space is an ownership boundary that needed no schema change, that scope has to sit in both the key and the column on both reads and writes, the three team roles enforced at two points with a build-breaking cross-check between them, and why the team assertion had to be a new type rather than a field added to the old one. Chapter 27 (`26-sync`) fixes the direction convention settled 2026-08-25 (`prerequisite_of` reads forward, `derives_from` and `inherits_from` read backward), the causal cone built from relations rather than a fourth clock, and the verdict order: causal order first, then cones, then density, never a metric. Chapter 28 (`27-infrastructure`) covers topic-driven density from the hub layout preset and the Gaussian verdict (rejected as a way to place Nodes, its radial ramp skipped as redundant with degree, kept only as a proposed overlay layer never deployed). Gap closed 2026-09-16: `vinc.book.27-infrastructure.en`'s stored text had broken off mid-sentence in section 4 of 8 ("...could be mod"); sections 4 through 8 (the rest of the Gaussian verdict, density does not explain cause, layout as a function, proximity is not evidence and density is not importance, and the Part 3 to Part 4 hand-off) were reconstructed from the Korean source and the English twin now reads complete and verified. VINC is spelled Vinc throughout and the English twins carry no em dash where their text survives.

Every input condition 7 named is therefore supplied: conditions 1 through 6 closed on 2026-09-04, the production-path RRF correction and the VNNI reading arrived as ruling material on 2026-09-03, and this is the last one. The measurement also carries a consequence the earlier framing could not have: at 1408 MiB the container has 640 MiB left, which is below every reranker resident set measured here, so executing the fleet rebuild forecloses reranker co-residency in the same container. That is ruling material in the same sense as the RRF correction, not a new condition, and it does not touch adoption, which decision A approved on 2026-08-30.

b.title: Measured 2026-09-10 on PR Vinc#301: a newly added query bound its primary-key predicate with logical slugs, so in a PK-namespaced store, where that column holds owner\x1fid, not one row matched. The symptom was the exact defect the branch existed to fix (an empty domain on every semantic hit), reached by a second route, and it was green on the core job and red only on core-pkns. The remedy is the idiom the rest of api/query.py already uses, pkns.keys(owner, ids); the read hook strips the keys back on the way out, so only the binding side is ever wrong. What this shows is that the two-job CI structure is load-bearing rather than redundant: a PK binding mistake produces empty results, not an exception, and the unnamespaced job cannot see it at all.

b.title: Written 2026-09-17 under VIN-49 (run oc-20260917-vin49-2): Part 4 (Chapters 29 to 34, slots vinc.book.28-performance to 33-measurement-before-decision) rewritten in Korean and English against the measured corpus rather than against the earlier prose, to the standard Parts 0 to 3 were rewritten to on 2026-09-16. The 2026-09-04 draft argued the right principles from no sources: it carried no chapter numbers, no numbered sections, no chapter-to-chapter hand-offs, spelled Vinc as VINC, used guillemets and em dashes, was filed under vinc/product with part2 tags, and stated its measurements without the runs they came from ("around 25 seconds", "some models took more than three times longer", "as low as 0.472 from 0.670"). Every factual sentence now traces to a graph document. Chapter 29 opens from Chapter 28's Part 3 close and fixes the conditions: the same-fixture rule and the ban on comparing absolute scores across fixtures, the four language axes with ko2en named as load-bearing, the two rounds that measured the wrong thing and said nothing (the first embedding round whose Korean queries were drawn from ASCII titles and filenames and therefore contained zero Korean characters, and the rebuild rehearsal's first evaluation reporting recall 0.0 because the harness read doc_id from a vector_search that returns id), the eleven-item record-these-fields list, the same-moment A/B against two measurements days apart, the cheapest gate first (two candidates screened against their model cards on 2026-09-07 before any fixture was built, both failed, and two of the plan's own premises were wrong), and the rule that a run states what it does not support. Chapter 30 gives calls-to-resolution with latency excluded by definition, the frozen arm policies, the four aggregates (baseline 15 calls 9 useful 40 percent 6 of 7; chain arm 10 calls 40 percent 5 of 7; brief-first 16 calls 62.5 percent 5 of 7; brief with a search in front 20 calls 70 percent), brief as a composite containing search rather than its competitor, target node kind as the axis that displaced question shape (Concept 6 of 6, Decision 2 of 2, Record 0 of 5, Episode 0 of 1) with the status misreporting a loader refusal as a failure to match, the payload crossover at about fifteen links (7,697 B at 0.73 percent used against 1,406 B at 12.66 percent; search flat at 7.7 KB, brief linear at about 455 B per link, the 208-character figure a floor not an envelope), attribution as the axis the chain arm cannot enter at all, and the Record and Episode branches shipped and verified live 2026-09-02 with the title-language tie-break left open by decision. Chapter 31 carries the nDCG@10 table (English-only 0.669/0.347/0.460, multilingual 0.636/0.670/0.658, vendor int8 0.574/0.472/0.508) stated as a trade rather than an improvement, the vendor int8 collapse traced to quantization without range reduction saturating the accumulator on a processor without the newer instruction extension and the self-built rebuild restoring Korean to 0.669, parent-and-child vectors with averaging measured below baseline (0.535 against 0.601 and 0.659) and the link-loss window that inflates links by up to 137 percent instead of restoring them, the cross-lingual numbers from the rebuild rehearsal, the artifact table with the 570 MB against 2.27 GB floor in a one-gibibyte container, and two honest notes: the cross-encoder is measured and not deployed pending a second container, and the 1024-dimensional candidate is ruled adopted with execution remaining while the shipped model is still 768. Chapter 32 prices the change: the dimension as a storage contract, provision at the new width returning all 31 statements and raising nothing while leaving the column where it was, the conversion error arriving only after every vector has already been deleted, the desktop vector table structurally empty so the fleet rebuild is one hub store, the four-step rebuild contract, the same-moment A/B where correctness cost 2.57 seconds against a refill of 410 to 1345 seconds, the encode bill (0.80 against 0.23 chunks per second, 3.5x, roughly 1.8 hours for 1500 chunks and 12 hours for 10,000), concurrency memory-bound at about 83 percent scaling, rollback as another rebuild with zero metadata mismatches after two of them, interruption safety once index build moved before re-embedding, and the metadata gap that was larger than the rebuild because backup restore and device migration had been losing the same tables all along. Chapter 33 collects the silent failures: the arm that did not run (8 fused, 4 timed out), the top-agree gate that fired 0 times in 75 queries because its threshold was pinned to a module constant of 60 against a pool production fuses at 20, and which once fixed skips 11 of 75 with numbers identical to always-reranking to three decimals, the status that misreported its own failure and the fix that moved it from loud to silent with a characterization test asserting the wrong answer, the edge evidence accepted and dropped with empty warnings and no partial flag, the English twin of Chapter 28 stored cut off mid-sentence in section 4 of 8 and reading as prose, the validity filter that turned an honest choose into an unearned resolved on one of six unanswerable questions, do not pick when it is ambiguous, and recovery as a measured axis. Chapter 34 gives the ordering: the decision its own conditions overturned, the measurement gate between result and decision, the six questions that precede it, the corrected recommendation list that ranked the symptom above the cause because it was proposed without reading the code, a plan's premises decaying like any other claim, the output being a record first and a decision second, the same ordering inside an Agent, and Part 4's mixed verdicts stated as mixed. All fourteen documents were read back after writing and each returned verified true on its first read with no truncation. Slot numbers still diverge from chapter numbers after Chapter 22, so the Chapter column of vinc.book.index remains the authority. Topics are authored at write time (vinc/product/book/part2 for Chapters 29 to 34), Vinc is spelled Vinc, and the English twins carry no em dash.

b.title: Written 2026-09-16: Part 3 (Chapters 24 to 28) rewritten in Korean and English, restructured into numbered sections with each chapter opening from the one before it, and Chapter 24 first working out what Chapter 6 announced and Chapter 18 already used as a search filter. Chapter 24 (`23-temporal`) names the three axes content, graph and valid time; states that an unstated window reads as current rather than historical, measured against the hub the day the policy was adopted (38 percent of Records then carried no start; 747 of 748 had one filled by that evening); splits validity by kind (71 of the 177 live Decisions carried a window as of 2026-09-11, 106 did not); and states two gaps rather than hiding them: document chunks carry no validity and the desktop app draws no interval on any card. Chapter 25 (`24-view`) gives Scope and Viewpoint as two axes neither can move, shape as kind across all four viewpoints with the 2026-08 two-day episode where 2D quietly stopped agreeing with that contract, line width traded for ink density carrying confidence, and the closed-encoding-versus-open-intensity split that decides what a shared pack can and cannot remap. Chapter 26 (`25-space`) states a space is an ownership boundary that needed no schema change, that scope has to sit in both the key and the column on both reads and writes, the three team roles enforced at two points with a build-breaking cross-check between them, and why the team assertion had to be a new type rather than a field added to the old one. Chapter 27 (`26-sync`) fixes the direction convention settled 2026-08-25 (`prerequisite_of` reads forward, `derives_from` and `inherits_from` read backward), the causal cone built from relations rather than a fourth clock, and the verdict order: causal order first, then cones, then density, never a metric. Chapter 28 (`27-infrastructure`) covers topic-driven density from the hub layout preset and the Gaussian verdict (rejected as a way to place Nodes, its radial ramp skipped as redundant with degree, kept only as a proposed overlay layer never deployed). Gap closed 2026-09-16: `vinc.book.27-infrastructure.en`'s stored text had broken off mid-sentence in section 4 of 8 ("...could be mod"); sections 4 through 8 (the rest of the Gaussian verdict, density does not explain cause, layout as a function, proximity is not evidence and density is not importance, and the Part 3 to Part 4 hand-off) were reconstructed from the Korean source and the English twin now reads complete and verified. VINC is spelled Vinc throughout and the English twins carry no em dash where their text survives.

b.title: Written 2026-09-16: Part 2 (Chapters 16 to 23) rewritten in Korean and English, restructured into numbered sections with each chapter opening from a hand-off out of the one before it (16 from Part 1's close, 21 from Chapter 7's principle, the rest from their immediate predecessor). Node-candidacy and the cross-language findings that Chapter 16 had carried alongside fusion were moved out to Chapter 18, so search-and-fusion (16) and resolution (18) each state their subject once instead of twice. Chapter 16 now says plainly that the cross-encoder reranker is measured (the disagreement gate loses nothing when skipped, and its value concentrates on cross-lingual questions) but not deployed, waiting on a second container beside the encoder. Chapter 17 covers parent-and-child vectors, the encoder as the one process holding the model, the multilingual model's self-built int8 quantization, and the 2026-09-11 dimension-contract rebuild from 768 to 1024 dimensions. Chapter 18 carries the N1 measurements: the candidate pool as a ceiling that a deeper search barely moves, the two-token confidence bar, the node semantic arm's margin (not absolute distance) as the deciding signal, choose rather than resolved as the product's actual behavior on three of four gold questions, and the answerability gate that ships off because its rule and its exam share an author. Chapter 19 states that brief generates nothing and only quotes, with three statuses and the Option C (material on a tied choose) left off by default. Chapter 20 covers the two transports over one dispatcher, the three entry paths with the owner always taken from authenticated identity, space as a call argument defaulting to personal since 2026-08-31, mandatory safety annotations, and states plainly that no call log exists yet. Chapter 21 gives a role's schema (tier, rung as a level rather than a model name, mission, reads, gates, never) and the four-role default roster; Chapter 22 (`21b-role-contract`) gives the verify tier's never-edit-never-escalate rule and the pull, gen and check verbs that keep execution shells honest against the graph. Chapter 23 (`22-provenance`) states that the evidence and confidence columns held zero of eighty relations before the same-sentence rule backfilled them, capped at 0.9 confidence pending human confirmation. VINC is spelled Vinc throughout and the English twins carry no em dash.

Chapter 20 covers the two transports over one dispatcher, the three entry paths with the owner always taken from authenticated identity, space as a call argument defaulting to personal since 2026-08-31, mandatory safety annotations, and states plainly that no call log exists yet. Chapter 23 (`22-provenance`) states that the evidence and confidence columns held zero of eighty relations before the same-sentence rule backfilled them, capped at 0.9 confidence pending human confirmation. VINC is spelled Vinc throughout and the English twins carry no em dash.

The 2026-09-04 draft argued the right principles from no sources: it carried no chapter numbers, no numbered sections, no chapter-to-chapter hand-offs, spelled Vinc as VINC, used guillemets and em dashes, was filed under vinc/product with part2 tags, and stated its measurements without the runs they came from ("around 25 seconds", "some models took more than three times longer", "as low as 0.472 from 0.670"). Every factual sentence now traces to a graph document. Chapter 29 opens from Chapter 28's Part 3 close and fixes the conditions: the same-fixture rule and the ban on comparing absolute scores across fixtures, the four language axes with ko2en named as load-bearing, the two rounds that measured the wrong thing and said nothing (the first embedding round whose Korean queries were drawn from ASCII titles and filenames and therefore contained zero Korean characters, and the rebuild rehearsal's first evaluation reporting recall 0.0 because the harness read doc_id from a vector_search that returns id), the eleven-item record-these-fields list, the same-moment A/B against two measurements days apart, the cheapest gate first (two candidates screened against their model cards on 2026-09-07 before any fixture was built, both failed, and two of the plan's own premises were wrong), and the rule that a run states what it does not support. Chapter 30 gives calls-to-resolution with latency excluded by definition, the frozen arm policies, the four aggregates (baseline 15 calls 9 useful 40 percent 6 of 7; chain arm 10 calls 40 percent 5 of 7; brief-first 16 calls 62.5 percent 5 of 7; brief with a search in front 20 calls 70 percent), brief as a composite containing search rather than its competitor, target node kind as the axis that displaced question shape (Concept 6 of 6, Decision 2 of 2, Record 0 of 5, Episode 0 of 1) with the status misreporting a loader refusal as a failure to match, the payload crossover at about fifteen links (7,697 B at 0.73 percent used against 1,406 B at 12.66 percent; search flat at 7.7 KB, brief linear at about 455 B per link, the 208-character figure a floor not an envelope), attribution as the axis the chain arm cannot enter at all, and the Record and Episode branches shipped and verified live 2026-09-02 with the title-language tie-break left open by decision. Chapter 31 carries the nDCG@10 table (English-only 0.669/0.347/0.460, multilingual 0.636/0.670/0.658, vendor int8 0.574/0.472/0.508) stated as a trade rather than an improvement, the vendor int8 collapse traced to quantization without range reduction saturating the accumulator on a processor without the newer instruction extension and the self-built rebuild restoring Korean to 0.669, parent-and-child vectors with averaging measured below baseline (0.535 against 0.601 and 0.659) and the link-loss window that inflates links by up to 137 percent instead of restoring them, the cross-lingual numbers from the rebuild rehearsal, the artifact table with the 570 MB against 2.27 GB floor in a one-gibibyte container, and two honest notes: the cross-encoder is measured and not deployed pending a second container, and the 1024-dimensional candidate is ruled adopted with execution remaining while the shipped model is still 768. Chapter 32 prices the change: the dimension as a storage contract, provision at the new width returning all 31 statements and raising nothing while leaving the column where it was, the conversion error arriving only after every vector has already been deleted, the desktop vector table structurally empty so the fleet rebuild is one hub store, the four-step rebuild contract, the same-moment A/B where correctness cost 2.57 seconds against a refill of 410 to 1345 seconds, the encode bill (0.80 against 0.23 chunks per second, 3.5x, roughly 1.8 hours for 1500 chunks and 12 hours for 10,000), concurrency memory-bound at about 83 percent scaling, rollback as another rebuild with zero metadata mismatches after two of them, interruption safety once index build moved before re-embedding, and the metadata gap that was larger than the rebuild because backup restore and device migration had been losing the same tables all along. Chapter 33 collects the silent failures: the arm that did not run (8 fused, 4 timed out), the top-agree gate that fired 0 times in 75 queries because its threshold was pinned to a module constant of 60 against a pool production fuses at 20, and which once fixed skips 11 of 75 with numbers identical to always-reranking to three decimals, the status that misreported its own failure and the fix that moved it from loud to silent with a characterization test asserting the wrong answer, the edge evidence accepted and dropped with empty warnings and no partial flag, the English twin of Chapter 28 stored cut off mid-sentence in section 4 of 8 and reading as prose, the validity filter that turned an honest choose into an unearned resolved on one of six unanswerable questions, do not pick when it is ambiguous, and recovery as a measured axis. b.title: Written 2026-09-16: Part 2 (Chapters 16 to 23) rewritten in Korean and English, restructured into numbered sections with each chapter opening from a hand-off out of the one before it (16 from Part 1's close, 21 from Chapter 7's principle, the rest from their immediate predecessor). Node-candidacy and the cross-language findings that Chapter 16 had carried alongside fusion were moved out to Chapter 18, so search-and-fusion (16) and resolution (18) each state their subject once instead of twice. Chapter 16 now says plainly that the cross-encoder reranker is measured (the disagreement gate loses nothing when skipped, and its value concentrates on cross-lingual questions) but not deployed, waiting on a second container beside the encoder. Chapter 17 covers parent-and-child vectors, the encoder as the one process holding the model, the multilingual model's self-built int8 quantization, and the 2026-09-11 dimension-contract rebuild from 768 to 1024 dimensions. Chapter 18 carries the N1 measurements: the candidate pool as a ceiling that a deeper search barely moves, the two-token confidence bar, the node semantic arm's margin (not absolute distance) as the deciding signal, choose rather than resolved as the product's actual behavior on three of four gold questions, and the answerability gate that ships off because its rule and its exam share an author. Chapter 19 states that brief generates nothing and only quotes, with three statuses and the Option C (material on a tied choose) left off by default. Chapter 20 covers the two transports over one dispatcher, the three entry paths with the owner always taken from authenticated identity, space as a call argument defaulting to personal since 2026-08-31, mandatory safety annotations, and states plainly that no call log exists yet. Chapter 21 gives a role's schema (tier, rung as a level rather than a model name, mission, reads, gates, never) and the four-role default roster; Chapter 22 (`21b-role-contract`) gives the verify tier's never-edit-never-escalate rule and the pull, gen and check verbs that keep execution shells honest against the graph. Chapter 23 (`22-provenance`) states that the evidence and confidence columns held zero of eighty relations before the same-sentence rule backfilled them, capped at 0.9 confidence pending human confirmation. VINC is spelled Vinc throughout and the English twins carry no em dash.

b.title: Written 2026-09-17 under VIN-49 (run oc-20260917-vin49-2): Part 4 (Chapters 29 to 34, slots vinc.book.28-performance to 33-measurement-before-decision) rewritten in Korean and English against the measured corpus rather than against the earlier prose, to the standard Parts 0 to 3 were rewritten to on 2026-09-16. The 2026-09-04 draft argued the right principles from no sources: it carried no chapter numbers, no numbered sections, no chapter-to-chapter hand-offs, spelled Vinc as VINC, used guillemets and em dashes, was filed under vinc/product with part2 tags, and stated its measurements without the runs they came from ("around 25 seconds", "some models took more than three times longer", "as low as 0.472 from 0.670"). Every factual sentence now traces to a graph document. Chapter 29 opens from Chapter 28's Part 3 close and fixes the conditions: the same-fixture rule and the ban on comparing absolute scores across fixtures, the four language axes with ko2en named as load-bearing, the two rounds that measured the wrong thing and said nothing (the first embedding round whose Korean queries were drawn from ASCII titles and filenames and therefore contained zero Korean characters, and the rebuild rehearsal's first evaluation reporting recall 0.0 because the harness read doc_id from a vector_search that returns id), the eleven-item record-these-fields list, the same-moment A/B against two measurements days apart, the cheapest gate first (two candidates screened against their model cards on 2026-09-07 before any fixture was built, both failed, and two of the plan's own premises were wrong), and the rule that a run states what it does not support. Chapter 30 gives calls-to-resolution with latency excluded by definition, the frozen arm policies, the four aggregates (baseline 15 calls 9 useful 40 percent 6 of 7; chain arm 10 calls 40 percent 5 of 7; brief-first 16 calls 62.5 percent 5 of 7; brief with a search in front 20 calls 70 percent), brief as a composite containing search rather than its competitor, target node kind as the axis that displaced question shape (Concept 6 of 6, Decision 2 of 2, Record 0 of 5, Episode 0 of 1) with the status misreporting a loader refusal as a failure to match, the payload crossover at about fifteen links (7,697 B at 0.73 percent used against 1,406 B at 12.66 percent; search flat at 7.7 KB, brief linear at about 455 B per link, the 208-character figure a floor not an envelope), attribution as the axis the chain arm cannot enter at all, and the Record and Episode branches shipped and verified live 2026-09-02 with the title-language tie-break left open by decision. Chapter 31 carries the nDCG@10 table (English-only 0.669/0.347/0.460, multilingual 0.636/0.670/0.658, vendor int8 0.574/0.472/0.508) stated as a trade rather than an improvement, the vendor int8 collapse traced to quantization without range reduction saturating the accumulator on a processor without the newer instruction extension and the self-built rebuild restoring Korean to 0.669, parent-and-child vectors with averaging measured below baseline (0.535 against 0.601 and 0.659) and the link-loss window that inflates links by up to 137 percent instead of restoring them, the cross-lingual numbers from the rebuild rehearsal, the artifact table with the 570 MB against 2.27 GB floor in a one-gibibyte container, and two honest notes: the cross-encoder is measured and not deployed pending a second container, and the 1024-dimensional candidate is ruled adopted with execution remaining while the shipped model is still 768. Chapter 32 prices the change: the dimension as a storage contract, provision at the new width returning all 31 statements and raising nothing while leaving the column where it was, the conversion error arriving only after every vector has already been deleted, the desktop vector table structurally empty so the fleet rebuild is one hub store, the four-step rebuild contract, the same-moment A/B where correctness cost 2.57 seconds against a refill of 410 to 1345 seconds, the encode bill (0.80 against 0.23 chunks per second, 3.5x, roughly 1.8 hours for 1500 chunks and 12 hours for 10,000), concurrency memory-bound at about 83 percent scaling, rollback as another rebuild with zero metadata mismatches after two of them, interruption safety once index build moved before re-embedding, and the metadata gap that was larger than the rebuild because backup restore and device migration had been losing the same tables all along. Chapter 33 collects the silent failures: the arm that did not run (8 fused, 4 timed out), the top-agree gate that fired 0 times in 75 queries because its threshold was pinned to a module constant of 60 against a pool production fuses at 20, and which once fixed skips 11 of 75 with numbers identical to always-reranking to three decimals, the status that misreported its own failure and the fix that moved it from loud to silent with a characterization test asserting the wrong answer, the edge evidence accepted and dropped with empty warnings and no partial flag, the English twin of Chapter 28 stored cut off mid-sentence in section 4 of 8 and reading as prose, the validity filter that turned an honest choose into an unearned resolved on one of six unanswerable questions, do not pick when it is ambiguous, and recovery as a measured axis. Chapter 34 gives the ordering: the decision its own conditions overturned, the measurement gate between result and decision, the six questions that precede it, the corrected recommendation list that ranked the symptom above the cause because it was proposed without reading the code, a plan's premises decaying like any other claim, the output being a record first and a decision second, the same ordering inside an Agent, and Part 4's mixed verdicts stated as mixed. All fourteen documents were read back after writing and each returned verified true on its first read with no truncation. Slot numbers still diverge from chapter numbers after Chapter 22, so the Chapter column of vinc.book.index remains the authority. Topics are authored at write time (vinc/product/book/part2 for Chapters 29 to 34), Vinc is spelled Vinc, and the English twins carry no em dash.

b.title: Written 2026-09-17 under VIN-49 (run oc-20260917-vin49-2): Part 4 (Chapters 29 to 34, slots vinc.book.28-performance to 33-measurement-before-decision) rewritten in Korean and English against the measured corpus rather than against the earlier prose, to the standard Parts 0 to 3 were rewritten to on 2026-09-16. The 2026-09-04 draft argued the right principles from no sources: it carried no chapter numbers, no numbered sections, no chapter-to-chapter hand-offs, spelled Vinc as VINC, used guillemets and em dashes, was filed under vinc/product with part2 tags, and stated its measurements without the runs they came from ("around 25 seconds", "some models took more than three times longer", "as low as 0.472 from 0.670"). Every factual sentence now traces to a graph document. Chapter 29 opens from Chapter 28's Part 3 close and fixes the conditions: the same-fixture rule and the ban on comparing absolute scores across fixtures, the four language axes with ko2en named as load-bearing, the two rounds that measured the wrong thing and said nothing (the first embedding round whose Korean queries were drawn from ASCII titles and filenames and therefore contained zero Korean characters, and the rebuild rehearsal's first evaluation reporting recall 0.0 because the harness read doc_id from a vector_search that returns id), the eleven-item record-these-fields list, the same-moment A/B against two measurements days apart, the cheapest gate first (two candidates screened against their model cards on 2026-09-07 before any fixture was built, both failed, and two of the plan's own premises were wrong), and the rule that a run states what it does not support. Chapter 30 gives calls-to-resolution with latency excluded by definition, the frozen arm policies, the four aggregates (baseline 15 calls 9 useful 40 percent 6 of 7; chain arm 10 calls 40 percent 5 of 7; brief-first 16 calls 62.5 percent 5 of 7; brief with a search in front 20 calls 70 percent), brief as a composite containing search rather than its competitor, target node kind as the axis that displaced question shape (Concept 6 of 6, Decision 2 of 2, Record 0 of 5, Episode 0 of 1) with the status misreporting a loader refusal as a failure to match, the payload crossover at about fifteen links (7,697 B at 0.73 percent used against 1,406 B at 12.66 percent; search flat at 7.7 KB, brief linear at about 455 B per link, the 208-character figure a floor not an envelope), attribution as the axis the chain arm cannot enter at all, and the Record and Episode branches shipped and verified live 2026-09-02 with the title-language tie-break left open by decision. Chapter 31 carries the nDCG@10 table (English-only 0.669/0.347/0.460, multilingual 0.636/0.670/0.658, vendor int8 0.574/0.472/0.508) stated as a trade rather than an improvement, the vendor int8 collapse traced to quantization without range reduction saturating the accumulator on a processor without the newer instruction extension and the self-built rebuild restoring Korean to 0.669, parent-and-child vectors with averaging measured below baseline (0.535 against 0.601 and 0.659) and the link-loss window that inflates links by up to 137 percent instead of restoring them, the cross-lingual numbers from the rebuild rehearsal, the artifact table with the 570 MB against 2.27 GB floor in a one-gibibyte container, and two honest notes: the cross-encoder is measured and not deployed pending a second container, and the 1024-dimensional candidate is ruled adopted with execution remaining while the shipped model is still 768. Chapter 32 prices the change: the dimension as a storage contract, provision at the new width returning all 31 statements and raising nothing while leaving the column where it was, the conversion error arriving only after every vector has already been deleted, the desktop vector table structurally empty so the fleet rebuild is one hub store, the four-step rebuild contract, the same-moment A/B where correctness cost 2.57 seconds against a refill of 410 to 1345 seconds, the encode bill (0.80 against 0.23 chunks per second, 3.5x, roughly 1.8 hours for 1500 chunks and 12 hours for 10,000), concurrency memory-bound at about 83 percent scaling, rollback as another rebuild with zero metadata mismatches after two of them, interruption safety once index build moved before re-embedding, and the metadata gap that was larger than the rebuild because backup restore and device migration had been losing the same tables all along. Chapter 33 collects the silent failures: the arm that did not run (8 fused, 4 timed out), the top-agree gate that fired 0 times in 75 queries because its threshold was pinned to a module constant of 60 against a pool production fuses at 20, and which once fixed skips 11 of 75 with numbers identical to always-reranking to three decimals, the status that misreported its own failure and the fix that moved it from loud to silent with a characterization test asserting the wrong answer, the edge evidence accepted and dropped with empty warnings and no partial flag, the English twin of Chapter 28 stored cut off mid-sentence in section 4 of 8 and reading as prose, the validity filter that turned an honest choose into an unearned resolved on one of six unanswerable questions, do not pick when it is ambiguous, and recovery as a measured axis. Chapter 34 gives the ordering: the decision its own conditions overturned, the measurement gate between result and decision, the six questions that precede it, the corrected recommendation list that ranked the symptom above the cause because it was proposed without reading the code, a plan's premises decaying like any other claim, the output being a record first and a decision second, the same ordering inside an Agent, and Part 4's mixed verdicts stated as mixed. All fourteen documents were read back after writing and each returned verified true on its first read with no truncation. Slot numbers still diverge from chapter numbers after Chapter 22, so the Chapter column of vinc.book.index remains the authority. Topics are authored at write time (vinc/product/book/part2 for Chapters 29 to 34), Vinc is spelled Vinc, and the English twins carry no em dash.

b.title: Failure traced 2026-09-11: an agent reported bge-m3 adoption as an open question and offered to author the decision, when decision:bge-m3-adoption had approved it on 2026-08-30 and only condition 7 of the separate execution decision was open. The source was one clause of a plan document that compresses both decisions into 'approved in principle, waits on the owner's ruling', which is true and reads as a single undecided thing. The decision node was one hop away and was never opened, although the same plan's house rule 1 is to read the records before the documents and the agent had transcribed that rule into the document minutes earlier. Two mechanisms, both reusable. First, having read a text closely feels like having verified it: attention on a document tells you what it says, not whether it holds. Second and sharper, the error was expressed as a frame (these two are one decision) rather than a claim, and a frame has no truth value to look up, so it never triggers the check that every falsifiable claim in the same session did trigger. The node had even anticipated the opposite misreading in a prop written for readers, so opening it would have prevented either direction.

b.title: Written 2026-09-17 under VIN-49 (run oc-20260917-vin49-2): Part 4 (Chapters 29 to 34, slots vinc.book.28-performance to 33-measurement-before-decision) rewritten in Korean and English against the measured corpus rather than against the earlier prose, to the standard Parts 0 to 3 were rewritten to on 2026-09-16. The 2026-09-04 draft argued the right principles from no sources: it carried no chapter numbers, no numbered sections, no chapter-to-chapter hand-offs, spelled Vinc as VINC, used guillemets and em dashes, was filed under vinc/product with part2 tags, and stated its measurements without the runs they came from ("around 25 seconds", "some models took more than three times longer", "as low as 0.472 from 0.670"). Every factual sentence now traces to a graph document. Chapter 29 opens from Chapter 28's Part 3 close and fixes the conditions: the same-fixture rule and the ban on comparing absolute scores across fixtures, the four language axes with ko2en named as load-bearing, the two rounds that measured the wrong thing and said nothing (the first embedding round whose Korean queries were drawn from ASCII titles and filenames and therefore contained zero Korean characters, and the rebuild rehearsal's first evaluation reporting recall 0.0 because the harness read doc_id from a vector_search that returns id), the eleven-item record-these-fields list, the same-moment A/B against two measurements days apart, the cheapest gate first (two candidates screened against their model cards on 2026-09-07 before any fixture was built, both failed, and two of the plan's own premises were wrong), and the rule that a run states what it does not support. Chapter 30 gives calls-to-resolution with latency excluded by definition, the frozen arm policies, the four aggregates (baseline 15 calls 9 useful 40 percent 6 of 7; chain arm 10 calls 40 percent 5 of 7; brief-first 16 calls 62.5 percent 5 of 7; brief with a search in front 20 calls 70 percent), brief as a composite containing search rather than its competitor, target node kind as the axis that displaced question shape (Concept 6 of 6, Decision 2 of 2, Record 0 of 5, Episode 0 of 1) with the status misreporting a loader refusal as a failure to match, the payload crossover at about fifteen links (7,697 B at 0.73 percent used against 1,406 B at 12.66 percent; search flat at 7.7 KB, brief linear at about 455 B per link, the 208-character figure a floor not an envelope), attribution as the axis the chain arm cannot enter at all, and the Record and Episode branches shipped and verified live 2026-09-02 with the title-language tie-break left open by decision. Chapter 31 carries the nDCG@10 table (English-only 0.669/0.347/0.460, multilingual 0.636/0.670/0.658, vendor int8 0.574/0.472/0.508) stated as a trade rather than an improvement, the vendor int8 collapse traced to quantization without range reduction saturating the accumulator on a processor without the newer instruction extension and the self-built rebuild restoring Korean to 0.669, parent-and-child vectors with averaging measured below baseline (0.535 against 0.601 and 0.659) and the link-loss window that inflates links by up to 137 percent instead of restoring them, the cross-lingual numbers from the rebuild rehearsal, the artifact table with the 570 MB against 2.27 GB floor in a one-gibibyte container, and two honest notes: the cross-encoder is measured and not deployed pending a second container, and the 1024-dimensional candidate is ruled adopted with execution remaining while the shipped model is still 768. Chapter 32 prices the change: the dimension as a storage contract, provision at the new width returning all 31 statements and raising nothing while leaving the column where it was, the conversion error arriving only after every vector has already been deleted, the desktop vector table structurally empty so the fleet rebuild is one hub store, the four-step rebuild contract, the same-moment A/B where correctness cost 2.57 seconds against a refill of 410 to 1345 seconds, the encode bill (0.80 against 0.23 chunks per second, 3.5x, roughly 1.8 hours for 1500 chunks and 12 hours for 10,000), concurrency memory-bound at about 83 percent scaling, rollback as another rebuild with zero metadata mismatches after two of them, interruption safety once index build moved before re-embedding, and the metadata gap that was larger than the rebuild because backup restore and device migration had been losing the same tables all along. Chapter 33 collects the silent failures: the arm that did not run (8 fused, 4 timed out), the top-agree gate that fired 0 times in 75 queries because its threshold was pinned to a module constant of 60 against a pool production fuses at 20, and which once fixed skips 11 of 75 with numbers identical to always-reranking to three decimals, the status that misreported its own failure and the fix that moved it from loud to silent with a characterization test asserting the wrong answer, the edge evidence accepted and dropped with empty warnings and no partial flag, the English twin of Chapter 28 stored cut off mid-sentence in section 4 of 8 and reading as prose, the validity filter that turned an honest choose into an unearned resolved on one of six unanswerable questions, do not pick when it is ambiguous, and recovery as a measured axis. Chapter 34 gives the ordering: the decision its own conditions overturned, the measurement gate between result and decision, the six questions that precede it, the corrected recommendation list that ranked the symptom above the cause because it was proposed without reading the code, a plan's premises decaying like any other claim, the output being a record first and a decision second, the same ordering inside an Agent, and Part 4's mixed verdicts stated as mixed. All fourteen documents were read back after writing and each returned verified true on its first read with no truncation. Slot numbers still diverge from chapter numbers after Chapter 22, so the Chapter column of vinc.book.index remains the authority. Topics are authored at write time (vinc/product/book/part2 for Chapters 29 to 34), Vinc is spelled Vinc, and the English twins carry no em dash.

b.title: Re-verified 2026-09-11 against the current trees and the live hub: three of the items the 2026-08-18 audit left open are closed. H1, the global node primary-key namespace that allowed slug squatting and silent cross-tenant write loss, shipped as PK namespacing and the hub runs with VINC_PK_NAMESPACED on (read from the container app's environment), with a dedicated core-pkns CI job holding it. H2, the pack zip bomb, is merged (MAX_ENTRIES and MAX_UNCOMPRESSED are read from the central directory before any inflate). H3, the redeemable revoked invite, is merged: the accept route checks inv.status is sent before consuming the token, with the reason written beside it. M1 is no longer 'zero owner references' either, since theme_store now derives an owner-scoped theme id, though whether that closes the vocabulary-pollution path was not re-checked. M2, the single unnonced assertion in front of /internal that does not sign the body, was not re-examined and should be read as still open.

b.title: Written 2026-09-16: Part 3 (Chapters 24 to 28) rewritten in Korean and English, restructured into numbered sections with each chapter opening from the one before it, and Chapter 24 first working out what Chapter 6 announced and Chapter 18 already used as a search filter. Chapter 24 (`23-temporal`) names the three axes content, graph and valid time; states that an unstated window reads as current rather than historical, measured against the hub the day the policy was adopted (38 percent of Records then carried no start; 747 of 748 had one filled by that evening); splits validity by kind (71 of the 177 live Decisions carried a window as of 2026-09-11, 106 did not); and states two gaps rather than hiding them: document chunks carry no validity and the desktop app draws no interval on any card. Chapter 25 (`24-view`) gives Scope and Viewpoint as two axes neither can move, shape as kind across all four viewpoints with the 2026-08 two-day episode where 2D quietly stopped agreeing with that contract, line width traded for ink density carrying confidence, and the closed-encoding-versus-open-intensity split that decides what a shared pack can and cannot remap. Chapter 26 (`25-space`) states a space is an ownership boundary that needed no schema change, that scope has to sit in both the key and the column on both reads and writes, the three team roles enforced at two points with a build-breaking cross-check between them, and why the team assertion had to be a new type rather than a field added to the old one. Chapter 27 (`26-sync`) fixes the direction convention settled 2026-08-25 (`prerequisite_of` reads forward, `derives_from` and `inherits_from` read backward), the causal cone built from relations rather than a fourth clock, and the verdict order: causal order first, then cones, then density, never a metric. Chapter 28 (`27-infrastructure`) covers topic-driven density from the hub layout preset and the Gaussian verdict (rejected as a way to place Nodes, its radial ramp skipped as redundant with degree, kept only as a proposed overlay layer never deployed). Gap closed 2026-09-16: `vinc.book.27-infrastructure.en`'s stored text had broken off mid-sentence in section 4 of 8 ("...could be mod"); sections 4 through 8 (the rest of the Gaussian verdict, density does not explain cause, layout as a function, proximity is not evidence and density is not importance, and the Part 3 to Part 4 hand-off) were reconstructed from the Korean source and the English twin now reads complete and verified. VINC is spelled Vinc throughout and the English twins carry no em dash where their text survives.

b.title: Written 2026-09-17 under VIN-49 (run oc-20260917-vin49-2): Part 4 (Chapters 29 to 34, slots vinc.book.28-performance to 33-measurement-before-decision) rewritten in Korean and English against the measured corpus rather than against the earlier prose, to the standard Parts 0 to 3 were rewritten to on 2026-09-16. The 2026-09-04 draft argued the right principles from no sources: it carried no chapter numbers, no numbered sections, no chapter-to-chapter hand-offs, spelled Vinc as VINC, used guillemets and em dashes, was filed under vinc/product with part2 tags, and stated its measurements without the runs they came from ("around 25 seconds", "some models took more than three times longer", "as low as 0.472 from 0.670"). Every factual sentence now traces to a graph document. Chapter 29 opens from Chapter 28's Part 3 close and fixes the conditions: the same-fixture rule and the ban on comparing absolute scores across fixtures, the four language axes with ko2en named as load-bearing, the two rounds that measured the wrong thing and said nothing (the first embedding round whose Korean queries were drawn from ASCII titles and filenames and therefore contained zero Korean characters, and the rebuild rehearsal's first evaluation reporting recall 0.0 because the harness read doc_id from a vector_search that returns id), the eleven-item record-these-fields list, the same-moment A/B against two measurements days apart, the cheapest gate first (two candidates screened against their model cards on 2026-09-07 before any fixture was built, both failed, and two of the plan's own premises were wrong), and the rule that a run states what it does not support. Chapter 30 gives calls-to-resolution with latency excluded by definition, the frozen arm policies, the four aggregates (baseline 15 calls 9 useful 40 percent 6 of 7; chain arm 10 calls 40 percent 5 of 7; brief-first 16 calls 62.5 percent 5 of 7; brief with a search in front 20 calls 70 percent), brief as a composite containing search rather than its competitor, target node kind as the axis that displaced question shape (Concept 6 of 6, Decision 2 of 2, Record 0 of 5, Episode 0 of 1) with the status misreporting a loader refusal as a failure to match, the payload crossover at about fifteen links (7,697 B at 0.73 percent used against 1,406 B at 12.66 percent; search flat at 7.7 KB, brief linear at about 455 B per link, the 208-character figure a floor not an envelope), attribution as the axis the chain arm cannot enter at all, and the Record and Episode branches shipped and verified live 2026-09-02 with the title-language tie-break left open by decision. Chapter 31 carries the nDCG@10 table (English-only 0.669/0.347/0.460, multilingual 0.636/0.670/0.658, vendor int8 0.574/0.472/0.508) stated as a trade rather than an improvement, the vendor int8 collapse traced to quantization without range reduction saturating the accumulator on a processor without the newer instruction extension and the self-built rebuild restoring Korean to 0.669, parent-and-child vectors with averaging measured below baseline (0.535 against 0.601 and 0.659) and the link-loss window that inflates links by up to 137 percent instead of restoring them, the cross-lingual numbers from the rebuild rehearsal, the artifact table with the 570 MB against 2.27 GB floor in a one-gibibyte container, and two honest notes: the cross-encoder is measured and not deployed pending a second container, and the 1024-dimensional candidate is ruled adopted with execution remaining while the shipped model is still 768. Chapter 32 prices the change: the dimension as a storage contract, provision at the new width returning all 31 statements and raising nothing while leaving the column where it was, the conversion error arriving only after every vector has already been deleted, the desktop vector table structurally empty so the fleet rebuild is one hub store, the four-step rebuild contract, the same-moment A/B where correctness cost 2.57 seconds against a refill of 410 to 1345 seconds, the encode bill (0.80 against 0.23 chunks per second, 3.5x, roughly 1.8 hours for 1500 chunks and 12 hours for 10,000), concurrency memory-bound at about 83 percent scaling, rollback as another rebuild with zero metadata mismatches after two of them, interruption safety once index build moved before re-embedding, and the metadata gap that was larger than the rebuild because backup restore and device migration had been losing the same tables all along. Chapter 33 collects the silent failures: the arm that did not run (8 fused, 4 timed out), the top-agree gate that fired 0 times in 75 queries because its threshold was pinned to a module constant of 60 against a pool production fuses at 20, and which once fixed skips 11 of 75 with numbers identical to always-reranking to three decimals, the status that misreported its own failure and the fix that moved it from loud to silent with a characterization test asserting the wrong answer, the edge evidence accepted and dropped with empty warnings and no partial flag, the English twin of Chapter 28 stored cut off mid-sentence in section 4 of 8 and reading as prose, the validity filter that turned an honest choose into an unearned resolved on one of six unanswerable questions, do not pick when it is ambiguous, and recovery as a measured axis. Chapter 34 gives the ordering: the decision its own conditions overturned, the measurement gate between result and decision, the six questions that precede it, the corrected recommendation list that ranked the symptom above the cause because it was proposed without reading the code, a plan's premises decaying like any other claim, the output being a record first and a decision second, the same ordering inside an Agent, and Part 4's mixed verdicts stated as mixed. All fourteen documents were read back after writing and each returned verified true on its first read with no truncation. Slot numbers still diverge from chapter numbers after Chapter 22, so the Chapter column of vinc.book.index remains the authority. Topics are authored at write time (vinc/product/book/part2 for Chapters 29 to 34), Vinc is spelled Vinc, and the English twins carry no em dash.

b.title: Written 2026-09-17 under VIN-49 (run oc-20260917-vin49-2): Part 4 (Chapters 29 to 34, slots vinc.book.28-performance to 33-measurement-before-decision) rewritten in Korean and English against the measured corpus rather than against the earlier prose, to the standard Parts 0 to 3 were rewritten to on 2026-09-16. The 2026-09-04 draft argued the right principles from no sources: it carried no chapter numbers, no numbered sections, no chapter-to-chapter hand-offs, spelled Vinc as VINC, used guillemets and em dashes, was filed under vinc/product with part2 tags, and stated its measurements without the runs they came from ("around 25 seconds", "some models took more than three times longer", "as low as 0.472 from 0.670"). Every factual sentence now traces to a graph document. Chapter 29 opens from Chapter 28's Part 3 close and fixes the conditions: the same-fixture rule and the ban on comparing absolute scores across fixtures, the four language axes with ko2en named as load-bearing, the two rounds that measured the wrong thing and said nothing (the first embedding round whose Korean queries were drawn from ASCII titles and filenames and therefore contained zero Korean characters, and the rebuild rehearsal's first evaluation reporting recall 0.0 because the harness read doc_id from a vector_search that returns id), the eleven-item record-these-fields list, the same-moment A/B against two measurements days apart, the cheapest gate first (two candidates screened against their model cards on 2026-09-07 before any fixture was built, both failed, and two of the plan's own premises were wrong), and the rule that a run states what it does not support. Chapter 30 gives calls-to-resolution with latency excluded by definition, the frozen arm policies, the four aggregates (baseline 15 calls 9 useful 40 percent 6 of 7; chain arm 10 calls 40 percent 5 of 7; brief-first 16 calls 62.5 percent 5 of 7; brief with a search in front 20 calls 70 percent), brief as a composite containing search rather than its competitor, target node kind as the axis that displaced question shape (Concept 6 of 6, Decision 2 of 2, Record 0 of 5, Episode 0 of 1) with the status misreporting a loader refusal as a failure to match, the payload crossover at about fifteen links (7,697 B at 0.73 percent used against 1,406 B at 12.66 percent; search flat at 7.7 KB, brief linear at about 455 B per link, the 208-character figure a floor not an envelope), attribution as the axis the chain arm cannot enter at all, and the Record and Episode branches shipped and verified live 2026-09-02 with the title-language tie-break left open by decision. Chapter 31 carries the nDCG@10 table (English-only 0.669/0.347/0.460, multilingual 0.636/0.670/0.658, vendor int8 0.574/0.472/0.508) stated as a trade rather than an improvement, the vendor int8 collapse traced to quantization without range reduction saturating the accumulator on a processor without the newer instruction extension and the self-built rebuild restoring Korean to 0.669, parent-and-child vectors with averaging measured below baseline (0.535 against 0.601 and 0.659) and the link-loss window that inflates links by up to 137 percent instead of restoring them, the cross-lingual numbers from the rebuild rehearsal, the artifact table with the 570 MB against 2.27 GB floor in a one-gibibyte container, and two honest notes: the cross-encoder is measured and not deployed pending a second container, and the 1024-dimensional candidate is ruled adopted with execution remaining while the shipped model is still 768. Chapter 32 prices the change: the dimension as a storage contract, provision at the new width returning all 31 statements and raising nothing while leaving the column where it was, the conversion error arriving only after every vector has already been deleted, the desktop vector table structurally empty so the fleet rebuild is one hub store, the four-step rebuild contract, the same-moment A/B where correctness cost 2.57 seconds against a refill of 410 to 1345 seconds, the encode bill (0.80 against 0.23 chunks per second, 3.5x, roughly 1.8 hours for 1500 chunks and 12 hours for 10,000), concurrency memory-bound at about 83 percent scaling, rollback as another rebuild with zero metadata mismatches after two of them, interruption safety once index build moved before re-embedding, and the metadata gap that was larger than the rebuild because backup restore and device migration had been losing the same tables all along. Chapter 33 collects the silent failures: the arm that did not run (8 fused, 4 timed out), the top-agree gate that fired 0 times in 75 queries because its threshold was pinned to a module constant of 60 against a pool production fuses at 20, and which once fixed skips 11 of 75 with numbers identical to always-reranking to three decimals, the status that misreported its own failure and the fix that moved it from loud to silent with a characterization test asserting the wrong answer, the edge evidence accepted and dropped with empty warnings and no partial flag, the English twin of Chapter 28 stored cut off mid-sentence in section 4 of 8 and reading as prose, the validity filter that turned an honest choose into an unearned resolved on one of six unanswerable questions, do not pick when it is ambiguous, and recovery as a measured axis. Chapter 34 gives the ordering: the decision its own conditions overturned, the measurement gate between result and decision, the six questions that precede it, the corrected recommendation list that ranked the symptom above the cause because it was proposed without reading the code, a plan's premises decaying like any other claim, the output being a record first and a decision second, the same ordering inside an Agent, and Part 4's mixed verdicts stated as mixed. All fourteen documents were read back after writing and each returned verified true on its first read with no truncation. Slot numbers still diverge from chapter numbers after Chapter 22, so the Chapter column of vinc.book.index remains the authority. Topics are authored at write time (vinc/product/book/part2 for Chapters 29 to 34), Vinc is spelled Vinc, and the English twins carry no em dash.
