a.title: Written 2026-09-17 under VIN-49 (run oc-20260917-vin49-2): Part 4 (Chapters 29 to 34, slots vinc.book.28-performance to 33-measurement-before-decision) rewritten in Korean and English against the measured corpus rather than against the earlier prose, to the standard Parts 0 to 3 were rewritten to on 2026-09-16. The 2026-09-04 draft argued the right principles from no sources: it carried no chapter numbers, no numbered sections, no chapter-to-chapter hand-offs, spelled Vinc as VINC, used guillemets and em dashes, was filed under vinc/product with part2 tags, and stated its measurements without the runs they came from ("around 25 seconds", "some models took more than three times longer", "as low as 0.472 from 0.670"). Every factual sentence now traces to a graph document. Chapter 29 opens from Chapter 28's Part 3 close and fixes the conditions: the same-fixture rule and the ban on comparing absolute scores across fixtures, the four language axes with ko2en named as load-bearing, the two rounds that measured the wrong thing and said nothing (the first embedding round whose Korean queries were drawn from ASCII titles and filenames and therefore contained zero Korean characters, and the rebuild rehearsal's first evaluation reporting recall 0.0 because the harness read doc_id from a vector_search that returns id), the eleven-item record-these-fields list, the same-moment A/B against two measurements days apart, the cheapest gate first (two candidates screened against their model cards on 2026-09-07 before any fixture was built, both failed, and two of the plan's own premises were wrong), and the rule that a run states what it does not support. Chapter 30 gives calls-to-resolution with latency excluded by definition, the frozen arm policies, the four aggregates (baseline 15 calls 9 useful 40 percent 6 of 7; chain arm 10 calls 40 percent 5 of 7; brief-first 16 calls 62.5 percent 5 of 7; brief with a search in front 20 calls 70 percent), brief as a composite containing search rather than its competitor, target node kind as the axis that displaced question shape (Concept 6 of 6, Decision 2 of 2, Record 0 of 5, Episode 0 of 1) with the status misreporting a loader refusal as a failure to match, the payload crossover at about fifteen links (7,697 B at 0.73 percent used against 1,406 B at 12.66 percent; search flat at 7.7 KB, brief linear at about 455 B per link, the 208-character figure a floor not an envelope), attribution as the axis the chain arm cannot enter at all, and the Record and Episode branches shipped and verified live 2026-09-02 with the title-language tie-break left open by decision. Chapter 31 carries the nDCG@10 table (English-only 0.669/0.347/0.460, multilingual 0.636/0.670/0.658, vendor int8 0.574/0.472/0.508) stated as a trade rather than an improvement, the vendor int8 collapse traced to quantization without range reduction saturating the accumulator on a processor without the newer instruction extension and the self-built rebuild restoring Korean to 0.669, parent-and-child vectors with averaging measured below baseline (0.535 against 0.601 and 0.659) and the link-loss window that inflates links by up to 137 percent instead of restoring them, the cross-lingual numbers from the rebuild rehearsal, the artifact table with the 570 MB against 2.27 GB floor in a one-gibibyte container, and two honest notes: the cross-encoder is measured and not deployed pending a second container, and the 1024-dimensional candidate is ruled adopted with execution remaining while the shipped model is still 768. Chapter 32 prices the change: the dimension as a storage contract, provision at the new width returning all 31 statements and raising nothing while leaving the column where it was, the conversion error arriving only after every vector has already been deleted, the desktop vector table structurally empty so the fleet rebuild is one hub store, the four-step rebuild contract, the same-moment A/B where correctness cost 2.57 seconds against a refill of 410 to 1345 seconds, the encode bill (0.80 against 0.23 chunks per second, 3.5x, roughly 1.8 hours for 1500 chunks and 12 hours for 10,000), concurrency memory-bound at about 83 percent scaling, rollback as another rebuild with zero metadata mismatches after two of them, interruption safety once index build moved before re-embedding, and the metadata gap that was larger than the rebuild because backup restore and device migration had been losing the same tables all along. Chapter 33 collects the silent failures: the arm that did not run (8 fused, 4 timed out), the top-agree gate that fired 0 times in 75 queries because its threshold was pinned to a module constant of 60 against a pool production fuses at 20, and which once fixed skips 11 of 75 with numbers identical to always-reranking to three decimals, the status that misreported its own failure and the fix that moved it from loud to silent with a characterization test asserting the wrong answer, the edge evidence accepted and dropped with empty warnings and no partial flag, the English twin of Chapter 28 stored cut off mid-sentence in section 4 of 8 and reading as prose, the validity filter that turned an honest choose into an unearned resolved on one of six unanswerable questions, do not pick when it is ambiguous, and recovery as a measured axis. Chapter 34 gives the ordering: the decision its own conditions overturned, the measurement gate between result and decision, the six questions that precede it, the corrected recommendation list that ranked the symptom above the cause because it was proposed without reading the code, a plan's premises decaying like any other claim, the output being a record first and a decision second, the same ordering inside an Agent, and Part 4's mixed verdicts stated as mixed. All fourteen documents were read back after writing and each returned verified true on its first read with no truncation. a.text: In the flat view leaves cluster around their branch, because extending them along a slice drew spiral arms instead of a hierarchy. Placing leaves by increasing radius inside an angular slice gives every branch one spiral arm, and together the arms read as a vortex: the eye sees a swirl rather than what sits under what.

b.title: Job identifiers are a counter and are not owner scoped
b.text: Job identifiers are a counter and are not owner scoped. Identifiers are a monotonic counter, so they are trivial to enumerate, and the lookup compares no owner, which exposes another tenant's ingest, synchronisation and backup results including file paths, counts and warnings.

b.title: Measured 2026-08-07: five store tests failed under PowerShell and passed under Git Bash on the same revision and machine, and the shell was a coincidence. The win_amd64 ladybug extensions (algo, fts, vector) need libssl-3-x64.dll and libcrypto-3-x64.dll under exactly those names, but the ladybug wheel ships only delvewheel-mangled copies in ladybug.libs (an upstream mismatch, not a Vinc defect); Git for Windows happens to keep both files unmangled in mingw64/bin, which is on Git Bash's PATH. Putting that directory on PATH makes LOAD EXTENSION vector succeed and settles it. What hid the cause was a second bug: the engine's error text is cp949 and the pybind boundary decoded strict UTF-8, so the real reason turned into a UnicodeDecodeError and vanished; _driver_error_text now recovers the original from UnicodeDecodeError.object and the message names the OpenSSL files and the PATH remedy.

b.title: Measured 2026-08-07: five store tests failed under PowerShell and passed under Git Bash on the same revision and machine, and the shell was a coincidence. The win_amd64 ladybug extensions (algo, fts, vector) need libssl-3-x64.dll and libcrypto-3-x64.dll under exactly those names, but the ladybug wheel ships only delvewheel-mangled copies in ladybug.libs (an upstream mismatch, not a Vinc defect); Git for Windows happens to keep both files unmangled in mingw64/bin, which is on Git Bash's PATH. Putting that directory on PATH makes LOAD EXTENSION vector succeed and settles it. What hid the cause was a second bug: the engine's error text is cp949 and the pybind boundary decoded strict UTF-8, so the real reason turned into a UnicodeDecodeError and vanished; _driver_error_text now recovers the original from UnicodeDecodeError.object and the message names the OpenSSL files and the PATH remedy.

One new record on vinc:store/embedded_schema.py now pairs as newer against four older records on that path covering mirror keying, ATTACHES_TO evidence, a schema version gap and the schema version number, and all five claims are simultaneously true. The pairing is co-location on a file, not disagreement, because subject_path resolves to a file while a record claims something about an aspect of one. Reading conflicts[].older as a list of invalidation candidates would retire true claims and catch no false ones. This is the second granularity defect on this field after the missing repository prefix, and unlike that one it has no obvious fix, since naming an aspect means coining stable names for parts of files.

M1 is no longer 'zero owner references' either, since theme_store now derives an owner-scoped theme id, though whether that closes the vocabulary-pollution path was not re-checked. M2, the single unnonced assertion in front of /internal that does not sign the body, was not re-examined and should be read as still open.

a.title: Written 2026-09-17 under VIN-49 (run oc-20260917-vin49-2): the closing (Chapter 35, vinc.book.35-cycle) rewritten in Korean and English so that it closes the arc vinc.book.index describes rather than restating it. It now opens from Chapter 34's last line (a measurement does not sit outside the system it measured), restates the storage question as the cycle the index prints, names each part by the problem it closed and the one it left exposed, and argues that no layer makes memory alone by citing Part 4's own findings as cases of one layer being correct while the system was wrong: a resolution path that worked on two node kinds and not the others, a semantic space that doubled one language by giving up part of another, and a gate whose correct-skip and never-fire states printed the same column. The eight questions a memory system must answer structurally are each tied to the mechanism behind them (kinds and relations, the evidence sentence, the fixture and its stated conditions, the failure cases and their dates, the Decision node and its window) instead of standing as a promise. A fourth section was added that the earlier draft had no equivalent for: the book is itself in the graph in both languages, carries its own provenance, goes stale, and several of its chapters were rewritten because the system moved and the text did not, which makes the final claim checkable rather than aspirational. The closing proposition is kept and its em dash removed. Both documents read back verified true on the first read, 3 chunks in English and 2 in Korean, and the topic is authored as vinc/product/book/part3.

The first full draft measured 1970 words of body text, about 8.6 minutes at 230 words per minute; one cutting pass took it to 1651 words, about 7.2 minutes. Getting to the roughly 1150 words that five minutes buys would mean dropping one of the four elements from each of the six primitives, and those four elements are criteria E1 to E4, which VIN-50 tests, whereas the five minutes is prose in plan section 4.2 and is not a numbered criterion. So four elements times six primitives won and the target was reported missed. The general shape worth carrying: when a plan states a size target and a criteria table states a content requirement, only one of them is machine-checked, and the unchecked one is the one that silently gets met by damaging the checked one unless the tension is measured and named.

b.title: Measured 2026-08-07: five store tests failed under PowerShell and passed under Git Bash on the same revision and machine, and the shell was a coincidence. The win_amd64 ladybug extensions (algo, fts, vector) need libssl-3-x64.dll and libcrypto-3-x64.dll under exactly those names, but the ladybug wheel ships only delvewheel-mangled copies in ladybug.libs (an upstream mismatch, not a Vinc defect); Git for Windows happens to keep both files unmangled in mingw64/bin, which is on Git Bash's PATH. Putting that directory on PATH makes LOAD EXTENSION vector succeed and settles it. What hid the cause was a second bug: the engine's error text is cp949 and the pybind boundary decoded strict UTF-8, so the real reason turned into a UnicodeDecodeError and vanished; _driver_error_text now recovers the original from UnicodeDecodeError.object and the message names the OpenSSL files and the PATH remedy.

a.title: Measured 2026-09-17 on /docs/concepts/ at Vinc-homepage 8ba33f4: the chosen primer shape and the five-minute reading target do not both fit, and the target is the one that gave way. The first full draft measured 1970 words of body text, about 8.6 minutes at 230 words per minute; one cutting pass took it to 1651 words, about 7.2 minutes. Getting to the roughly 1150 words that five minutes buys would mean dropping one of the four elements from each of the six primitives, and those four elements are criteria E1 to E4, which VIN-50 tests, whereas the five minutes is prose in plan section 4.2 and is not a numbered criterion. So four elements times six primitives won and the target was reported missed. The general shape worth carrying: when a plan states a size target and a criteria table states a content requirement, only one of them is machine-checked, and the unchecked one is the one that silently gets met by damaging the checked one unless the tension is measured and named.

b.title: Found 2026-09-17 implementing VIN-44: two strings that vinc.spec.docs-information-architecture-2026-09 states verbatim are forbidden by gate_copy, and both were caught by the gate rather than by review. First, the Korean title it gives for /docs/app/view/ is View 표면, but 표면 is a developer literal in Korean site copy and the site word is 화면 (vinc.spec.ui-copy-ko section 4, gate_copy rule ko-surface-rail); written as View 화면. Second, the book chapter 13 document slot carries a product noun the site retired (gate_copy rule en-product-noun), and a URL is copy, so that one chapter's slug comes from the chapter title rather than the slot name, giving /docs/book/ch13-concept-system/. The second is what the specification section 3.5 actually directs, which is that the slug comes from the chapter title; its own two worked examples happen to be slot names, so the rule only bites on this one chapter. Note also that an explanatory code comment naming the forbidden word trips the same gate, so the comment has to describe it without writing it.

a.title: Measured 2026-08-07: five store tests failed under PowerShell and passed under Git Bash on the same revision and machine, and the shell was a coincidence. The win_amd64 ladybug extensions (algo, fts, vector) need libssl-3-x64.dll and libcrypto-3-x64.dll under exactly those names, but the ladybug wheel ships only delvewheel-mangled copies in ladybug.libs (an upstream mismatch, not a Vinc defect); Git for Windows happens to keep both files unmangled in mingw64/bin, which is on Git Bash's PATH. Putting that directory on PATH makes LOAD EXTENSION vector succeed and settles it. What hid the cause was a second bug: the engine's error text is cp949 and the pybind boundary decoded strict UTF-8, so the real reason turned into a UnicodeDecodeError and vanished; _driver_error_text now recovers the original from UnicodeDecodeError.object and the message names the OpenSSL files and the PATH remedy.

a.title: Found 2026-09-17 implementing VIN-44: two strings that vinc.spec.docs-information-architecture-2026-09 states verbatim are forbidden by gate_copy, and both were caught by the gate rather than by review. First, the Korean title it gives for /docs/app/view/ is View 표면, but 표면 is a developer literal in Korean site copy and the site word is 화면 (vinc.spec.ui-copy-ko section 4, gate_copy rule ko-surface-rail); written as View 화면. Second, the book chapter 13 document slot carries a product noun the site retired (gate_copy rule en-product-noun), and a URL is copy, so that one chapter's slug comes from the chapter title rather than the slot name, giving /docs/book/ch13-concept-system/. The second is what the specification section 3.5 actually directs, which is that the slug comes from the chapter title; its own two worked examples happen to be slot names, so the rule only bites on this one chapter. Note also that an explanatory code comment naming the forbidden word trips the same gate, so the comment has to describe it without writing it.
